knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prefix trie for a fixed-arity finite relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tuple trie for \(T\) is a rooted directed tree with levels \(0,\ldots,n\). The root represents the empty prefix. For each represented prefix \(p=(a_1,\ldots,a_i)\), there is one node \(v_p\) at level \(i\); an edge labeled \(a_{i+1}\) joins \(v_p\) to \(v_{(p,a_{i+1})}\) exactly when that extended prefix occurs in some tuple of \(T\). A node at level \(n\) is terminal. Consequently, each root-to-terminal label sequence is exactly one tuple in \(T\), and common prefixes are stored once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tuple trie stores each occurring prefix once; its root-to-terminal label sequences are exactly the allowed tuples.
knowledge_statements.title: Tuple Tries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the Tuple Tries leaf, but it has no cited source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Compressed Tuple Sets
children.top_down_role: Shared or factored storage for tuple collections.

assumptions_latex: The relation \(T\) is finite and all tuples have the same arity \(n\).
Compression operations preserve the set of decoded root-to-terminal label sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Decoding the compressed structure yields exactly \(T\).

notation.meaning: set of tuples decoded from a representation

review_flags: Compression format is not uniquely fixed by the title or supplied locators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lossless compression of fixed-arity extensional relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compressed tuple set \(C(T)\) is a finite data structure obtained from an explicit tuple set by sharing repeated prefixes, suffixes, subgraphs, or label blocks, together with an unambiguous decoding rule. It is valid precisely when \[\operatorname{Dec}(C(T))=T.\] For constraint use, membership and support queries must interpret the decoded relation: a value \(a\in D_i\) is supported exactly when some decoded tuple \(t\in\operatorname{Dec}(C(T))\) satisfies \(t_i=a\) and \(t_j\in D_j\) for every \(j\). Compression may change storage and traversal costs but not relation semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compressed tuple set is any lossless shared representation whose decoded tuples equal the original finite relation and whose support queries use those same tuples.
knowledge_statements.title: Compressed Tuple Sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation establishes this broad notion of a compressed tuple set. The title does not uniquely determine which compression operations, decoding model, or supported query interface belong to the representation family.

children.title: Prefix-Sharing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Tuple structures where common prefixes govern compression effectiveness.

assumptions_latex: A finite tuple set \(T\) has arity \(n\).
For each \(i\), let \(P_i(T)\) be the set of distinct length-\(i\) prefixes occurring in \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A prefix trie has \(1+\sum_{i=1}^n|P_i(T)|\) nodes and at most \(n|T|+1\) nodes.

notation.meaning: set of occurring prefixes of length \(i\)

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports prefix-sharing storage bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage benefit from shared tuple prefixes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exact node count of the prefix trie is \[N_{\mathrm{trie}}=1+\sum_{i=1}^{n}|P_i(T)|.\] Since \(|P_i(T)|\leq |T|\), it follows that \(N_{\mathrm{trie}}\leq 1+n|T|\). Equality in the upper bound occurs when no two tuples share any nonempty prefix. Prefix sharing is strongest when many tuples have identical initial coordinates, because every common prefix contributes one node rather than one stored copy per tuple. Thus the compression gain is governed by the profile \((|P_1(T)|,\ldots,|P_n(T)|)\), not solely by \(|T|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trie size equals one plus the number of distinct prefixes at all depths, so compression improves exactly when tuples share many initial coordinate sequences.
knowledge_statements.title: Prefix-Sharing Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The trie node-count identity follows from the stated prefix model and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports its use as the asserted prefix-sharing complexity bound.

children.title: Short Tables
children.top_down_role: Compressed table representations using partial tuple specifications.

assumptions_latex: Variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) have universes \(U_1,\ldots,U_n\).
The allowed relation is \(R\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^n U_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A set of short tuples represents \(R\) exactly when the union of their cylinders equals \(R\).

notation.meaning: partial assignment called a short tuple

review_flags: No supplied locator directly defines short tables.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short tuples interpreted as partial assignments covering allowed tuples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A short tuple is a partial assignment \(s:I\to\bigcup_{i=1}^n U_i\), where \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(s(i)\in U_i\). Its cylinder is \[[s]=\{t\in\textstyle\prod_{i=1}^n U_i:t_i=s(i)\text{ for every }i\in I\}.\] It is valid for \(R\) when \([s]\subseteq R\). A short table \(S\) represents \(R\) exactly when every member is valid and \[R=\bigcup_{s\in S}[s].\] Coordinates outside \(I\) are unrestricted; therefore one short tuple can represent multiple full allowed tuples.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A short table covers an allowed relation by valid partial assignments, each standing for every full tuple that extends it.
knowledge_statements.title: Short Tables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cylinder definition is coherent, but short-table semantics can depend on the constraint literature's treatment of domains and omitted coordinates. A specialist source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Wildcard Tables
children.top_down_role: Table representations using symbols that cover multiple values.

assumptions_latex: Each coordinate \(i\) has a finite universe \(U_i\).
A distinguished wildcard symbol \(\ast\) is not contained in any \(U_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A wildcard table denotes the union of the Cartesian cylinders represented by its rows.

notation.meaning: wildcard symbol matching every value in a coordinate universe

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports wildcard-table semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cartesian-cylinder semantics for wildcard rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A wildcard row is \(w\in\prod_{i=1}^n(U_i\cup\{\ast\})\). Its denotation is \[\llbracket w\rrbracket=\{t\in\textstyle\prod_{i=1}^n U_i: w_i=\ast\text{ or }t_i=w_i\text{ for every }i\}.\] A finite wildcard table \(W\) denotes \(\llbracket W\rrbracket=\bigcup_{w\in W}\llbracket w\rrbracket\). It is an exact positive representation of a relation \(R\) when \(\llbracket W\rrbracket=R\). Under current domains \(D_i\), a row remains feasible exactly when every fixed entry belongs to its corresponding domain and every wildcard coordinate has nonempty domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each wildcard row denotes all full tuples matching its fixed entries; a wildcard table denotes the union of these row cylinders.
knowledge_statements.title: Wildcard Tables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The wildcard-row semantics are internally consistent and the representation kind fits, but no cited source with a specific locator supports the terminology or feasibility criterion.

children.title: Tuple-Coverage Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Compression, overlap, and filtering consequences of generalized tuple entries.

assumptions_latex: A finite relation \(R\) is represented by valid short tuples drawn from a candidate family \(\mathcal S\).
Each short tuple \(s\) has storage or filtering cost \(c_s\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimum-cost exact short-table construction is a weighted set-cover problem over the full tuples of \(R\).

notation.meaning: binary selection variable for short tuple \(s\)

review_flags: No supplied locator directly establishes the tuple-coverage formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted coverage formulation for choosing short tuples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Selecting an exact short-table cover can be formulated as \[\min\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}c_s y_s\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{s\in\mathcal S:t\in[s]}y_s\geq1\ \text{for every }t\in R,\qquad y_s\in\{0,1\}.\] Validity \([s]\subseteq R\) ensures that no selected short tuple introduces a forbidden full tuple, while the covering inequalities ensure that every allowed tuple is represented. Larger cylinders may reduce the number of stored rows, but their broad coverage can increase overlap and the work required by propagation; the costs \(c_s\) encode the chosen storage-filtering tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing valid short tuples to cover every allowed full tuple is weighted set cover, with row costs capturing storage and filtering tradeoffs.
knowledge_statements.title: Tuple-Coverage Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted set-cover formulation is valid under the stated finite candidate-family and additive-cost assumptions, but no source supports it or the propagation-work tradeoff. The selected representation kind is also questionable for an optimization formulation or tradeoff principle.

assumptions_latex: Variables are ordered as \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) with finite domains \(U_i\).
The diagram is a finite layered directed acyclic graph with one root and one terminal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented relation is exactly the set of label sequences on root-to-terminal paths.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly defines MDD representations for constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered deterministic MDD semantics for finite relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multi-valued decision diagram is a layered directed acyclic graph \(G=(V,E)\) whose layers are \(V_0,\ldots,V_n\), with a root in \(V_0\), a terminal in \(V_n\), and every edge from \(V_{i-1}\) to \(V_i\) labeled by an element of \(U_i\). In the deterministic form, no node has two outgoing edges with the same label. Its represented relation is \[R(G)=\{(\lambda(e_1),\ldots,\lambda(e_n)):(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\text{ is a root-to-terminal path}\}.\] Nodes with identical accepted suffix relations may be merged without changing \(R(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordered MDD is a layered labeled DAG whose root-to-terminal paths spell exactly the represented tuples; deterministic nodes have unique outgoing labels.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Valued Decision Diagrams

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The path-language definition is coherent, but the record mixes the generic MDD title with an ordered deterministic variant and a suffix-merging claim. A specialist citation must establish the intended local variant.

assumptions_latex: Variables are ordered as \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) over finite alphabets \(U_i\).
The representation is a layered labeled directed acyclic graph with designated root and terminal layers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A tuple is represented when at least one root-to-terminal path spells it.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports nondeterministic MDD semantics or terminology.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential path semantics for nondeterministic MDDs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nondeterministic MDD is a layered labeled directed acyclic graph \(G=(V,E)\) in which multiple edges leaving the same node may carry the same value, possibly reaching different successor nodes. A tuple \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) belongs to \(R(G)\) exactly when there exists a root-to-terminal path \((e_1,\ldots,e_n)\) satisfying \(\lambda(e_i)=t_i\) for every \(i\). Hence acceptance uses existential path semantics. Distinct paths may spell the same tuple, so path count need not equal \(|R(G)|\); removing all paths spelling a tuple removes that tuple from the represented relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nondeterministic MDD permits same-labeled outgoing alternatives and accepts a tuple when at least one root-to-terminal path spells it.
knowledge_statements.title: Nondeterministic MDD Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The existential path semantics are internally consistent, but no inspectable source supports the term nondeterministic MDD or the precise same-label branching convention used here.

children.title: Deterministic Automata
children.top_down_role: Single-successor transition representations for sequence constraints.

assumptions_latex: The alphabet \(\Sigma\) is finite.
Input words have arbitrary finite length unless a constraint fixes a sequence length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every word induces one run, and it is accepted exactly when the run ends in \(F\).
review_flags: The supplied locators do not directly support automata definitions in regular constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete deterministic finite automata for regular-language constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic finite automaton is a tuple \(A=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\), where \(Q\) is a finite state set, \(\Sigma\) is a finite alphabet, \(q_0\in Q\), \(F\subseteq Q\), and \(\delta:Q\times\Sigma\to Q\) is a total function. Extend \(\delta\) by \(\delta^\ast(q,\varepsilon)=q\) and \(\delta^\ast(q,wa)=\delta(\delta^\ast(q,w),a)\). The accepted language is \[L(A)=\{w\in\Sigma^\ast:\delta^\ast(q_0,w)\in F\}.\] Determinism means that each state-symbol pair has exactly one successor, so every input word has a unique run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic finite automaton has exactly one successor for each state-symbol pair and accepts precisely the words whose unique runs end in accepting states.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Automata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a standard complete-DFA definition and fits the leaf, but the candidate supplies no authoritative citation or specific locator as required.

children.title: Nondeterministic Automata
children.top_down_role: Multiple-successor transition representations for sequence constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Nondeterministic Automata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-word nondeterministic automata, allowing multiple initial states and transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nondeterministic finite automaton is a tuple \(A=(Q,\Sigma,\Delta,I,F)\), where \(Q\) and \(\Sigma\) are finite, \(\Delta\subseteq Q\times\Sigma\times Q\), \(I\subseteq Q\) is nonempty, and \(F\subseteq Q\). A run on \(w=a_1\cdots a_n\in\Sigma^*\) is \(q_0,\ldots,q_n\) satisfying \(q_0\in I\) and \((q_{i-1},a_i,q_i)\in\Delta\) for every \(i\). The word is accepted exactly when some run has \(q_n\in F\); the accepted language is \(L(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An NFA accepts a word when at least one transition-compatible run starts in an initial state and ends in an accepting state.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) and \(\Sigma\) are finite.
\(I\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(A)=\{w\in\Sigma^*: \text{an accepting run of }A\text{ on }w\text{ exists}\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and the definition kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable automata source is cited.

children.title: Determinization Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: State growth, transition density, and filtering implications.

knowledge_statements.title: Determinization Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset construction for finite-word nondeterministic automata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nondeterministic finite automaton \(A=(Q,\Sigma,\Delta,I,F)\), the subset construction produces a deterministic automaton whose states are reachable subsets \(S\subseteq Q\), whose initial state is \(I\), and whose transition is \(\delta_D(S,a)=\{q':\exists q\in S,\ (q,a,q')\in\Delta\}\). A subset is accepting exactly when it intersects \(F\). The resulting automaton recognizes \(L(A)\), has at most \(2^{|Q|}\) states, and this exponential worst-case state growth is tight over families of regular languages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Determinization preserves the language but can replace an NFA with exponentially many reachable subset states; this worst-case blowup is unavoidable.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a finite nondeterministic automaton without epsilon transitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(D)=L(A)\) and \(|Q_D|\le 2^{|Q|}\), with an asymptotically tight exponential worst case.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the determinization-tradeoff leaf, but the language-equivalence theorem and tight exponential lower bound require an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Layered Automaton Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acyclic position-layer expansion for a fixed-length regular constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an automaton \(A=(Q,\Sigma,\Delta,I,F)\) and variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), form a directed acyclic graph with vertices \((i,q)\) for \(i\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) and \(q\in Q\). For every \(a\in D(X_i)\) and \((q,a,q')\in\Delta\), add an arc labeled \(a\) from \((i-1,q)\) to \((i,q')\). Then an assignment \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) satisfies the regular-language constraint exactly when its labels form a path from some \((0,q_0)\), with \(q_0\in I\), to some \((n,q_n)\), with \(q_n\in F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-length regular constraint is represented by an acyclic layered graph whose accepting paths correspond exactly to feasible variable assignments.
assumptions_latex: \(D(X_i)\subseteq\Sigma\) for every \(i\).
\(A\) has no epsilon transitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\text{ is feasible}\iff\text{its labels define an initial-to-accepting layered path}\).

notation.meaning: automaton state q after i positions
current domain of the ith variable

knowledge_statements.title: Forward–Backward Reachability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-consistency filtering on the layered representation of a regular constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R_0^+=I\) and compute \(R_i^+=\{q':\exists q\in R_{i-1}^+,\exists a\in D(X_i),\ (q,a,q')\in\Delta\}\). Initialize \(R_n^-=F\) and compute backward \(R_{i-1}^-=\{q:\exists a\in D(X_i),\exists q'\in R_i^-,\ (q,a,q')\in\Delta\}\). Delete \(a\in D(X_i)\) unless some transition \((q,a,q')\in\Delta\) satisfies \(q\in R_{i-1}^+\) and \(q'\in R_i^-\). Repeat after deletions if the reachability sets were not recomputed from the final domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and backward reachable states identify exactly which variable values lie on a currently feasible accepting path.
assumptions_latex: \(D(X_i)\subseteq\Sigma\) for all positions.
The layered graph represents a finite automaton without epsilon transitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\in D(X_i)\text{ survives}\iff a\text{ labels an initial-to-accepting path through layer }i\).

notation.meaning: states reachable through the first i domains
states that can reach acceptance through the remaining domains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and forward–backward support test fit the leaf, but no propagation source with an inspectable algorithm or theorem locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Automaton Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worklist maintenance of layered path support after monotone domain deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain the currently supported layered arcs and, for each vertex, counts of supported incoming and outgoing arcs. When a value is removed from \(D(X_i)\), delete every layer-\(i\) arc carrying that value and place any vertex whose required count becomes zero on a worklist. Repeatedly delete arcs incident to a worklist vertex that is no longer reachable from an initial vertex or cannot reach an accepting vertex, updating neighboring counts. Remove a value when its final supporting arc disappears. Stop when the worklist is empty or an initial-to-accepting path is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental filtering propagates only reachability losses caused by domain deletions, removing values after their last accepting-path support disappears.
assumptions_latex: Domains shrink monotonically during the filtering episode.
Arc-support counts and boundary reachability are initially correct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{At termination, every retained value lies on a supported accepting path, or infeasibility is detected.}\)

notation.meaning: supported arcs between layers i−1 and i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the reachability/count invariants and arc-deletion rules are not specified precisely enough to establish correctness without the missing incremental-filtering source.

children.title: Cost Automaton Variants
children.top_down_role: Automaton representations carrying transition or state costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost Automaton Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive transition-cost automata over fixed-length variable sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cost automaton augments \(A=(Q,\Sigma,\Delta,I,F)\) with a transition cost \(c:\Delta\to\mathbb{R}\). The cost of a run \(\rho=(q_0,a_1,q_1),\ldots,(q_{n-1},a_n,q_n)\) is \(C(\rho)=\sum_{i=1}^n c(q_{i-1},a_i,q_i)\). For an assignment \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), its automaton cost is \(C_A(x)=\min\{C(\rho):\rho\text{ is an accepting run labeled }x\}\), with \(C_A(x)=+\infty\) when no accepting run exists. A cost-regular constraint additionally restricts or equates a cost variable to \(C_A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cost automaton assigns additive transition costs and maps each word to the minimum cost of any accepting run with that label.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a finite automaton.
Run costs are additive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_A(x)=\min_{\rho\text{ accepts }x}\sum_{e\in\rho}c(e)\).

notation.meaning: minimum accepting-run cost of assignment x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the minimum-run semantics and claimed cost-regular convention require a specifically located source.

children.title: Soft Automaton Variants
children.top_down_role: Automaton representations permitting quantified violations.

knowledge_statements.title: Soft Automaton Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty relaxation of regular-language membership using an explicitly chosen word distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(A)\subseteq\Sigma^*\) be regular and let \(d:\Sigma^*\times\Sigma^*\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a specified discrepancy measure. The soft automaton violation of a word \(x\) is \(v_A(x)=\min_{y\in L(A)}d(x,y)\). A soft regular constraint on variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) and violation variable \(V\) requires \(V\ge v_A(X_1\cdots X_n)\), or \(V=v_A(X_1\cdots X_n)\) in the exact-cost form. Substitution, insertion-deletion, and transition-penalty variants arise from different choices of \(d\) or an equivalent weighted automaton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A soft automaton permits nonaccepted words and measures their minimum specified discrepancy from an accepted word.
assumptions_latex: \(d(x,y)\ge0\) for all words.
\(d(x,y)=0\) exactly when \(x=y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_A(x)=0\iff x\in L(A)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but for an arbitrary discrepancy on an infinite regular language the displayed minimum need not be attained. A source is needed to identify the intended distance class and support a corrected formulation.

children.title: Violation–Cost Coupling
children.top_down_role: Relationships between accepted deviations and accumulated penalties.

knowledge_statements.title: Violation–Cost Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and bounded coupling between a soft violation measure and a cost variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_A(x)\) be the minimum violation cost assigned to word \(x\) by a nonnegative weighted soft automaton, and let \(V\) be its violation variable. Exact coupling imposes \(V=v_A(x)\); budget coupling imposes \(v_A(x)\le V\le B\). If every zero-cost accepting computation corresponds exactly to membership in the hard language \(L(A)\), then \(V=0\) certifies the hard regular constraint. For separable transition penalties, exact coupling is equivalently \(V=\min_{\rho\text{ accepting }x}\sum_{e\in\rho}c(e)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A violation variable equals or bounds the least automaton penalty; zero violation recovers the hard constraint when only valid words have zero cost.
assumptions_latex: \(c(e)\ge0\) for every weighted transition.
Zero-cost acceptance occurs exactly for words in \(L(A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V=v_A(x)\Longrightarrow (V=0\iff x\in L(A))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the coupling leaf, but the relation between soft computations, hard-language acceptance, and the final minimum-over-runs formula depends on an unstated weighted-automaton convention.

children.title: Sequence Constraints
children.top_down_role: Sequence-wide restrictions on designated value membership.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical fixed-window counting form of the global SEQUENCE constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be variables, let \(S\) be a distinguished set of values, and let \(1\le k\le n\) and \(0\le \ell\le u\le k\). The constraint \(\operatorname{SEQUENCE}(\ell,u,k,X,S)\) holds exactly when every consecutive window of length \(k\) contains between \(\ell\) and \(u\) variables assigned values in \(S\): \[\ell\le\sum_{j=i}^{i+k-1}\mathbf{1}[X_j\in S]\le u\qquad(i=1,\ldots,n-k+1).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every length-k consecutive window must contain between the prescribed lower and upper numbers of values from a distinguished set.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le k\le n\).
\(0\le\ell\le u\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall i\in\{1,\ldots,n-k+1\}:\ \ell\le\sum_{j=i}^{i+k-1}\mathbf{1}[X_j\in S]\le u\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The classical SEQUENCE definition is precise and the definition kind fits, but no authoritative global-constraint citation with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Sliding-Cardinality Constraints
children.top_down_role: Cardinality restrictions repeated across overlapping windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Sliding-Cardinality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Window-indexed cardinality bounds, generalizing fixed-parameter SEQUENCE.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be variables and \(S\) a distinguished value set. For each window \(W_r=\{s_r,\ldots,t_r\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), choose integer bounds \(0\le\ell_r\le u_r\le|W_r|\). The sliding-cardinality constraint holds exactly when \[\ell_r\le\sum_{j=s_r}^{t_r}\mathbf{1}[X_j\in S]\le u_r\qquad\text{for every }r.\] The classical sequence constraint is the special case containing every window of one fixed length with common bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each specified consecutive window has its own lower and upper bound on the number of variables taking distinguished values.
assumptions_latex: Each \(W_r\) is a nonempty consecutive index interval.
\(0\le\ell_r\le u_r\le|W_r|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall r:\ \ell_r\le\sum_{j\in W_r}\mathbf{1}[X_j\in S]\le u_r\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the proposed window-specific generalization and its designation as “sliding-cardinality” require a specifically located source.

children.title: Window-Overlap Effects
children.top_down_role: Propagation consequences of shared variables across neighboring windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Window-Overlap Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic coupling of adjacent equal-length cardinality windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(Y_j=\mathbf{1}[X_j\in S]\) and \(C_i=\sum_{j=i}^{i+k-1}Y_j\) for consecutive length-\(k\) windows. Adjacent counts obey \(C_{i+1}-C_i=Y_{i+k}-Y_i\), hence \(|C_{i+1}-C_i|\le1\). More generally, windows shifted by \(r\le k\) satisfy \(|C_{i+r}-C_i|\le r\). Thus overlapping-window bounds are coupled: fixing entering or leaving indicators can tighten neighboring counts, and independently feasible window intervals need not possess a jointly feasible binary sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping windows share variables, so adjacent counts differ only by the entering and leaving indicators and cannot be propagated independently.
assumptions_latex: All displayed windows have common length \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{i+1}=C_i-Y_i+Y_{i+k}\) and \(|C_{i+r}-C_i|\le r\) for \(0\le r\le k\).

notation.meaning: indicator of membership in the counted value set
cardinality of the window beginning at i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits and the adjacent-window identities are coherent, but the propagation and joint-feasibility claims lack an inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: Sliding-Sum Constraints
children.top_down_role: Numeric aggregate restrictions over moving windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Sliding-Sum Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-length consecutive-window bounds on sums of numeric variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be real- or integer-valued variables, let \(1\le k\le n\), and let \(L\le U\). The sliding-sum constraint holds exactly when every consecutive length-\(k\) window has a sum within the prescribed interval: \[L\le\sum_{j=i}^{i+k-1}X_j\le U\qquad(i=1,\ldots,n-k+1).\] With prefix sums \(P_0=0\) and \(P_i=\sum_{j=1}^iX_j\), the same constraint is represented by \(L\le P_{i+k-1}-P_{i-1}\le U\) for every admissible \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every consecutive window of a fixed length must have its variable sum between common lower and upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\in\mathbb{R}\) or \(X_i\in\mathbb{Z}\) consistently.
\(1\le k\le n\) and \(L\le U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall i\in\{1,\ldots,n-k+1\}:\ L\le\sum_{j=i}^{i+k-1}X_j\le U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits and the prefix-sum representation is internally consistent, but no authoritative sliding-sum source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: General Window Constraints
children.top_down_role: Local restrictions repeated over contiguous subsequences.

knowledge_statements.title: General Window Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted bounds over an arbitrary indexed family of sequence windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) with \(x_i\in D_i\subseteq\mathbb R\). Given an index set \(K\), windows \(W_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), coefficients \(a_{ki}\in\mathbb R\), and bounds \(L_k,U_k\in\mathbb R\) with \(L_k\le U_k\), the general window constraint is satisfied exactly when
\[L_k\le \sum_{i\in W_k}a_{ki}x_i\le U_k\qquad\text{for every }k\in K.\]
Windows may overlap and need not have equal size or be contiguous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every specified window must satisfy its own lower and upper bound on a weighted sum of the sequence variables.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\) and each \(D_i\subseteq\mathbb R\).
\(L_k\le U_k\) for every \(k\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is feasible if and only if \(L_k\le\sum_{i\in W_k}a_{ki}x_i\le U_k\) for all \(k\in K\).

notation.meaning: coefficient of position i in window k
permitted weighted-sum interval for window k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the General Window Constraints leaf, but it has no citation or inspectable locator. None of the inventoried sources specifically supports this global-constraint family.

children.title: Overlapping-Window Propagation
children.top_down_role: Cross-window filtering induced by shared positions.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping-Window Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound interval propagation through the common variables of two sum windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A,B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(T=A\cap B\), and suppose \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\). If \(L_A\le\sum_{i\in A}x_i\le U_A\) and \(L_B\le\sum_{i\in B}x_i\le U_B\), then every feasible assignment satisfies
\[\sum_{i\in T}x_i\in I_A\cap I_B,\]
where \(I_A=[L_A-\sum_{i\in A\setminus T}u_i,\ U_A-\sum_{i\in A\setminus T}\ell_i]\) and \(I_B=[L_B-\sum_{i\in B\setminus T}u_i,\ U_B-\sum_{i\in B\setminus T}\ell_i]\). An empty intersection certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds from each overlapping window induce bounds on their shared sum; intersecting them propagates information or detects infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\in A\cup B\).
Both displayed window-sum constraints hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in A\cap B}x_i\in I_A\cap I_B\); if \(I_A\cap I_B=\varnothing\), no feasible assignment exists.

notation.meaning: overlap-sum intervals inferred from the two windows

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval inference is sound and property is an appropriate content kind for this propagation leaf. An authoritative constraint-propagation source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Stretch Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions over maximal blocks of repeated values.

knowledge_statements.title: Stretch Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical value-dependent bounds on maximal constant stretches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in V^n\), and assign integers \(m_v,M_v\) with \(1\le m_v\le M_v\) to every \(v\in V\). A stretch is a maximal interval \([p,q]\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) on which \(x_p=\cdots=x_q=v\). The stretch constraint holds exactly when
\[m_v\le q-p+1\le M_v\]
for every stretch of value \(v\). Maximality means \(p=1\) or \(x_{p-1}\ne v\), and \(q=n\) or \(x_{q+1}\ne v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each maximal block of an equal value must have a length within the bounds assigned to that value.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in V^n\).
\(1\le m_v\le M_v\) for every \(v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every maximal \(v\)-stretch has length in \([m_v,M_v]\).

notation.meaning: minimum and maximum stretch lengths for value v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The value-dependent maximal-stretch definition is precise and locally appropriate, but no source supports that this is the intended classical Stretch constraint variant.

children.title: Run-Length Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on lengths of consecutive-value runs.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in V^n\).
\(R_v\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is specified for every \(v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q-p+1\in R_v\) for every maximal run \([p,q]\) of value \(v\).

notation.meaning: admissible run-length set for value v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible-length predicates for maximal runs in a finite sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in V^n\), let \(R_v\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be the admissible run lengths for value \(v\). A run-length constraint is satisfied precisely when every maximal interval \([p,q]\) with \(x_p=\cdots=x_q=v\) obeys
\[q-p+1\in R_v.\]
Equivalently, if \(0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_r=n\) are all run boundaries, then \(t_j-t_{j-1}\in R_{x_{t_{j-1}+1}}\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The length of every maximal constant run must belong to the admissible length set associated with its value.
knowledge_statements.title: Run-Length Constraints

children.title: Run-Boundary Reasoning
children.top_down_role: Filtering based on possible starts, ends, and adjacency of runs.

knowledge_statements.title: Run-Boundary Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-variable encoding of maximal constant runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in V^n\), introduce \(b_1=1\) and, for \(i=2,\ldots,n\), impose
\[b_i=1\iff x_i\ne x_{i-1}.\]
Then run starts are exactly the indices with \(b_i=1\). If consecutive starts are \(p<q\), the run starting at \(p\) has length \(q-p\); the final run starting at \(p\) has length \(n-p+1\). Consequently, domain-disjointness \(D(x_{i-1})\cap D(x_i)=\varnothing\) forces \(b_i=1\), while a forced equality forces \(b_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean boundary variables exactly identify value changes, represent run lengths, and propagate forced changes or equalities between adjacent positions.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in V\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The indices satisfying \(b_i=1\) are precisely the starts of the maximal constant runs of \(x\).

notation.meaning: indicator that a run starts at position i
current domain of sequence variable x_i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary-variable encoding is internally consistent and representation fits the reasoning leaf. Its encoding and propagation claims nevertheless require a relevant source with a specific locator.

children.title: Pattern Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on occurrence or avoidance of designated subsequences.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite alphabet.
\(L\subseteq V^*\) is specified independently of the assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assigned word \(x_1\cdots x_n\) belongs to \(L\).

notation.meaning: set of all finite words over V
optional set of forbidden contiguous patterns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sequence membership in a language specifying allowed patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be a finite alphabet and \(L\subseteq V^*\) a specified language, for example one recognized by a finite automaton. For sequence variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in V\), the pattern constraint associated with \(L\) holds exactly when
\[x_1x_2\cdots x_n\in L.\]
In the forbidden-factor variant, given \(F\subseteq V^*\), define \(L_F=\{w\in V^*: \text{no contiguous factor of }w\text{ belongs to }F\}\). Membership in \(L_F\) is then equivalent to requiring that no contiguous factor \(x_p\cdots x_q\) belong to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence satisfies the pattern constraint when its value word belongs to the specified language. In the forbidden-factor variant, this means that none of its contiguous factors is a designated forbidden word.
knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Constraints

children.title: Sequence-Precedence Constraints
children.top_down_role: Ordering restrictions among values or event classes in a sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Precedence Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered first occurrence of values in a sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in V^n\) and let \((v_1,\ldots,v_m)\) be distinct values. Define \(f(v)=\min\{i:x_i=v\}\), with \(f(v)=+\infty\) when \(v\) is absent. The sequence-precedence constraint holds exactly when, for every \(2\le j\le m\),
\[f(v_j)<+\infty\implies f(v_{j-1})<f(v_j).\]
Thus any occurrence of \(v_j\) requires an earlier occurrence of every preceding value in the ordered list.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever a listed value occurs, every earlier listed value must already have appeared, so first occurrences respect the prescribed order.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in V^n\).
\(v_1,\ldots,v_m\in V\) are pairwise distinct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(v_j)<+\infty\) implies \(f(v_1)<\cdots<f(v_j)\) for every \(j\).

notation.meaning: first position containing v, or positive infinity if absent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The first-occurrence semantics is coherent, and the adjacent implications entail the stated full precedence chain. The definition fits the leaf but lacks an authoritative global-constraint citation and locator.

children.title: Pattern–Precedence Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined pattern occurrence and ordering restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern–Precedence Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-automaton representation of simultaneous pattern and precedence requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L_P\subseteq V^*\) be recognized by a deterministic finite automaton \(A_P\), and let \(L_Q\subseteq V^*\) encode a fixed sequence-precedence requirement and be recognized by \(A_Q\). Form the synchronous product automaton whose state after reading a symbol \(v\) is
\[(q_P,q_Q)\longmapsto\bigl(\delta_P(q_P,v),\delta_Q(q_Q,v)\bigr),\]
with initial state \((q_P^0,q_Q^0)\) and accepting set \(F_P\times F_Q\). This product recognizes exactly \(L_P\cap L_Q\); hence one regular constraint enforces both the pattern and precedence constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting the pattern and precedence automata yields one product automaton whose accepted sequences satisfy both constraint families exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
\(A_P\) and \(A_Q\) are deterministic finite automata over \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(A_P\times A_Q)=L_P\cap L_Q\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The synchronous-product construction correctly represents conjunction by language intersection, and representation fits the interaction leaf. Sources are still needed both for the automata construction in this constraint context and for the regular-language encoding of the stated precedence requirement.

children.title: Temporal-Resource Scheduling Family
children.top_down_role: Activity representations, temporal-resource globals, propagation families, overload certificates, and resource extensions.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Propagation of one-machine and cumulative resource constraints

children.title: Fixed-Duration Activities
children.top_down_role: Scheduling representations for activities whose durations are fixed.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Duration Activities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval activity with a constant processing duration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A fixed-duration activity \(i\) is represented by a start-time variable \(s_i\), an end-time variable \(e_i\), and a prescribed constant duration \(p_i\ge0\), with the channeling equation
\[e_i=s_i+p_i.\]
Under the half-open interval convention, the activity occupies \([s_i,e_i)\). Consequently, whenever it is present, it executes for exactly \(p_i\) time units and is active at time \(t\) exactly when \(s_i\le t<e_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-duration activity occupies a half-open interval whose end equals its start plus a prescribed constant duration.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i,e_i\) lie in a common ordered time domain.
\(p_i\ge0\) is constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_i=s_i+p_i\), and the occupied interval is \([s_i,e_i)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-duration interval definition is standard and matches the leaf, including its explicit half-open convention. It has no relevant scheduling source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Variable-Duration Activities
children.top_down_role: Scheduling representations for activities whose durations remain variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Duration Activities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval activity whose duration is a decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A variable-duration activity \(i\) is represented by start, end, and duration variables \(s_i,e_i,d_i\), where \(d_i\in D_i\subseteq\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), together with
\[e_i=s_i+d_i.\]
Under the half-open interval convention, a present activity occupies \([s_i,e_i)\). Any additional mode, resource, or calendar restrictions may reduce \(D_i\), but feasibility always requires the selected duration and temporal endpoints to satisfy the channeling equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-duration activity selects a nonnegative duration from its domain, and its end time is channeled to start plus that duration.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i,e_i,d_i\) lie in compatible time domains.
\(D_i\subseteq\mathbb R_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_i\in D_i\) and \(e_i=s_i+d_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The variable-duration activity definition is internally consistent and appropriately distinguished from the fixed-duration case. A scheduling reference with a specific section, definition, or page locator is required.

children.title: Duration-Domain Channeling
children.top_down_role: Links between activity timing variables and duration domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Duration-Domain Channeling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact indicator encoding of a finite duration domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the duration domain of activity \(i\) be \(D_i=\{\delta_{i1},\ldots,\delta_{im}\}\). Introduce binary selectors \(y_{ik}\) and impose
\[\sum_{k=1}^{m}y_{ik}=1,\qquad d_i=\sum_{k=1}^{m}\delta_{ik}y_{ik},\qquad e_i=s_i+d_i.\]
Then exactly one admissible duration is selected. Conversely, every \(d_i\in D_i\) has a selector assignment satisfying these equations; if equal listed values are removed, that selector assignment is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-hot binary selectors choose exactly one duration-domain value and channel it to the duration and activity endpoint.
assumptions_latex: \(D_i\) is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The encoding is feasible exactly when \(d_i\in D_i\) and \(e_i=s_i+d_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-hot finite-domain encoding is exact under the stated binary-selector assumptions, and representation is the correct role for this channeling leaf. No scheduling or encoding source with a specific locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Optional Activities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activity interval controlled by a Boolean presence decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An optional activity \(i\) has a presence variable \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\), start \(s_i\), end \(e_i\), and duration \(d_i\ge0\). Its temporal relation is enforced conditionally:
\[z_i=1\implies e_i=s_i+d_i.\]
When \(z_i=1\), the activity occupies \([s_i,e_i)\) and participates in every scheduling constraint containing it. When \(z_i=0\), it contributes neither temporal occupation nor resource demand; its inactive endpoint values are semantically irrelevant unless separately constrained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presence variable determines whether an activity occupies time and consumes resources; its start–duration–end relation is required when present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(z_i=1\), then \(e_i=s_i+d_i\) and activity \(i\) occupies \([s_i,e_i)\); if \(z_i=0\), it is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The presence-controlled interval semantics is locally appropriate for Optional Activities, with absent endpoint values explicitly treated as irrelevant unless separately constrained. The record requires a source documenting optional-activity semantics and a specific locator.

assumptions_latex: Each interval activity has a presence indicator and, when present, finite start and end times.
The candidate alternatives belong to one common scheduling model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_0=\sum_{i=1}^{m}z_i\), with synchronized endpoints for the unique selected alternative.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-programming interval semantics with exactly one selected child whenever the master is present.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Alternative activities consist of a master interval \(a_0\) and candidate intervals \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\) satisfying \[z_0=\sum_{i=1}^{m}z_i.\] Consequently, absence of \(a_0\) forces every alternative to be absent, while presence of \(a_0\) selects exactly one index \(k\). For that selected index, the temporal extent is synchronized with the master: \[s_k=s_0,\qquad e_k=e_0.\] No endpoint condition is imposed by this template on an absent candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master activity is absent with all alternatives, or present with exactly one alternative having the same start and end times.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Activities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The alternative-activity semantics are plausible and fit the definition container, but no source supports the presence and endpoint-synchronization semantics. The symbols s_i and e_i also need explicit introduction.

assumptions_latex: Every interval has a presence indicator and finite endpoints when present.
At least one child is supplied to the span template.

notation.meaning: presence, start, and end of interval \(a_i\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval-variable span over the temporal hull of all present children.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A span activity \(a_0\) over children \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\) is governed by \[z_0=\max_{1\le i\le m}z_i.\] If \(z_0=1\), its endpoints are the temporal hull of the present children: \[s_0=\min_{i:z_i=1}s_i,\qquad e_0=\max_{i:z_i=1}e_i.\] Thus every present child lies within \([s_0,e_0]\), and the spanning interval is absent exactly when every child is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The span is present exactly when some child is present, and its interval is the smallest time interval containing all present children.
knowledge_statements.title: Span Activities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The span definition is mathematically coherent and matches the container, but its interval-presence and temporal-hull semantics have no cited source.

assumptions_latex: The activity set and precedence-arc set are finite.
Every activity has a start time and a fixed nonnegative duration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible schedules are precisely the solutions of \(s_j-s_i\ge p_i+\ell_{ij}\) for all \((i,j)\in E\).

notation.meaning: start time and duration of activity \(i\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finish-to-start precedence network with fixed activity durations and arc-specific minimum lags.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A precedence network is a directed graph \(G=(V,E)\) whose vertices are activities and whose arc \((i,j)\) requires activity \(j\) to start after completion of activity \(i\), possibly with lag \(\ell_{ij}\). Its feasible start-time vectors are \[\mathcal S(G)=\left\{s\in\mathbb R^{V}:s_j-s_i\ge p_i+\ell_{ij}\text{ for every }(i,j)\in E\right\}.\] With zero lags, each arc is the ordinary finish-to-start precedence condition \(s_j\ge s_i+p_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A precedence network represents activities as vertices and temporal ordering requirements as directed arcs imposing start-time difference inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Precedence Networks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finish-to-start network representation is precise and locally appropriate, but no source supports the chosen fixed-duration, arc-lag specialization.

children.title: Minimum Lags
children.top_down_role: Lower-bound separation requirements between scheduled activities.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum Lags
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic temporal-distance form; start-to-start and finish-to-start lags arise by choosing the time points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A minimum lag \(L_{ij}\) from time point \(t_i\) to time point \(t_j\) is the constraint \[t_j-t_i\ge L_{ij}.\] Equivalently, \(t_j\ge t_i+L_{ij}\). Positive values enforce a positive minimum separation, zero requires \(t_j\ge t_i\), and negative values permit \(t_j\) to precede \(t_i\) by at most \(-L_{ij}\) time units. For optional activities, the inequality is required only when both referenced time points are active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum lag requires the second time point to occur at least a prescribed amount after the first.
assumptions_latex: The referenced time points are defined whenever the associated activities are present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_j-t_i\ge L_{ij}\).

notation.meaning: selected time points of activities \(i\) and \(j\)

children.title: Maximum Lags
children.top_down_role: Upper-bound separation requirements between scheduled activities.

assumptions_latex: The referenced time points are defined whenever the associated activities are present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_j-t_i\le U_{ij}\).

notation.meaning: selected time points of activities \(i\) and \(j\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic temporal-distance form, conditional on presence when optional intervals supply the time points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A maximum lag \(U_{ij}\) from time point \(t_i\) to time point \(t_j\) is the constraint \[t_j-t_i\le U_{ij}.\] Equivalently, \(t_j\le t_i+U_{ij}\). It prevents the second event from occurring more than \(U_{ij}\) time units after the first; a negative value requires it to occur strictly earlier when time is continuous. For optional activities, the inequality is required only when both referenced time points are active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximum lag requires the second time point to occur no more than a prescribed amount after the first.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Lags

children.title: Two-Sided Lag Windows
children.top_down_role: Temporal relations combining lower and upper lag limits.

assumptions_latex: The lower and upper lags satisfy \(L_{ij}\le U_{ij}\).
The referenced time points are simultaneously defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{ij}\le t_j-t_i\le U_{ij}\).

notation.meaning: selected time points of activities \(i\) and \(j\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed two-sided temporal-distance window between a specified pair of event times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A two-sided lag window between \(t_i\) and \(t_j\) is the ranged temporal constraint \[L_{ij}\le t_j-t_i\le U_{ij}.\] It is exactly the conjunction of the corresponding minimum-lag and maximum-lag constraints. The admissible values of \(t_j\), conditional on \(t_i\), form the translated interval \([t_i+L_{ij},t_i+U_{ij}]\). The window is intrinsically inconsistent when \(L_{ij}>U_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-sided lag window confines the temporal separation of two events between specified lower and upper limits.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Lag Windows

children.title: Release-Date Bounds
children.top_down_role: Earliest-start restrictions for activities or events.

assumptions_latex: Activity \(i\) has a defined start time when it is present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i\ge r_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bound on an activity's start time, enforced conditionally for an optional activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A release-date bound for activity \(i\) is the lower-bound constraint \[s_i\ge r_i,\] where \(r_i\) is the earliest permitted start time. If the activity has fixed duration \(p_i\) and end time \(e_i=s_i+p_i\), the same condition is equivalently \(e_i\ge r_i+p_i\). For an optional activity, this bound applies whenever the activity is present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A release date is the earliest time at which an activity may start.
knowledge_statements.title: Release-Date Bounds

children.title: Deadline Bounds
children.top_down_role: Latest-completion restrictions for activities or events.

assumptions_latex: Activity \(i\) has a defined completion time when it is present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_i\le d_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper bound on completion time, distinct from a latest-start bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deadline bound for activity \(i\) is the upper-bound constraint \[e_i\le d_i,\] where \(d_i\) is the latest permitted completion time. If the activity has fixed duration \(p_i\) and \(e_i=s_i+p_i\), this is equivalently the latest-start bound \(s_i\le d_i-p_i\). For an optional activity, the bound applies whenever the activity is present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deadline is the latest time by which an activity must finish.
knowledge_statements.title: Deadline Bounds

children.title: Time-Window Domains
children.top_down_role: Permitted temporal regions bounded by scheduling limits.

assumptions_latex: Activity \(i\) has fixed duration \(p_i\ge0\).
Its release date and deadline are finite real numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i\in[r_i,d_i-p_i]\) and \(e_i\in[r_i+p_i,d_i]\).

notation.meaning: start, end, and duration of activity \(i\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-time domain induced by release, deadline, and fixed-duration constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed-duration activity satisfying \(e_i=s_i+p_i\), release date \(r_i\), and deadline \(d_i\), the time-window constraints \(s_i\ge r_i\) and \(e_i\le d_i\) induce \[s_i\in[r_i,d_i-p_i],\qquad e_i\in[r_i+p_i,d_i].\] In discrete time, these intervals are intersected with the scheduling time lattice. For an optional activity, these domains constrain its endpoints only when it is present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Release and deadline bounds restrict a fixed-duration activity's start and completion to corresponding closed time intervals.
knowledge_statements.title: Time-Window Domains

children.title: Window Feasibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundary cases where temporal windows become incompatible.

assumptions_latex: Activity \(i\) has fixed duration \(p_i\ge0\).
The only local temporal restrictions are release date \(r_i\) and deadline \(d_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The activity has a feasible placement if and only if \(r_i+p_i\le d_i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fixed-duration activity admits a start time satisfying \(s_i\ge r_i\) and \(s_i+p_i\le d_i\) if and only if \[r_i+p_i\le d_i,\] equivalently \(p_i\le w_i\). Equality leaves the unique placement \(s_i=r_i\). If \(r_i+p_i>d_i\), the start domain \([r_i,d_i-p_i]\) is empty, so a mandatory activity makes the model infeasible and an optional activity cannot be present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-duration activity fits its window exactly when its duration does not exceed the time from release to deadline.

assumptions_latex: All temporal constraints have been normalized to difference inequalities \(x_v-x_u\le c_{uv}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simple temporal-network propagation by shortest-path closure of difference constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite system of constraints \(x_v-x_u\le c_{uv}\). Build a directed graph containing arc \(u\to v\) of weight \(c_{uv}\), initialize \(d(u,u)=0\), arc distances to their weights, and all other distances to \(+\infty\). Compute all-pairs shortest-path closure. If some \(d(v,v)<0\), output infeasible. Otherwise output every implied bound \[x_v-x_u\le d(u,v),\] and intersect these bounds with the current event-time domains; stop when closure causes no further tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize temporal constraints as weighted arcs, compute shortest-path closure, tighten all implied time differences, and report infeasibility when a negative cycle appears.
knowledge_statements.title: Temporal-Distance Propagation Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The disjunctive graph is \(G=(V,A,E)\), where \(A\) contains fixed technological precedence arcs and \(E\) contains one undirected edge for each pair of operations requiring the same unary machine. Orienting every \(\{i,j\}\in E\) as either \(i\to j\) or \(j\to i\) selects the corresponding temporal order. An orientation is feasible when the resulting precedence digraph is acyclic; assigning each start time to the longest weighted path into its vertex, with vertex weight \(p_i\), then satisfies all selected precedences. Conversely, every feasible schedule orients each conflict edge from the earlier operation to the later one.

assumptions_latex: Each activity \(i\in J\) has release bound \(r_i\), deadline bound \(d_i\), and processing time \(p_i>0\).

\[
P(U)=\sum_{i\in U}p_i>d(U)-r(U)
\]
is a verifiable overload certificate: no pairwise nonoverlapping placement of all activities in \(U\) can respect their release and deadline bounds. Unary overload checking rejects the current domains whenever it finds such a subset.

\[
\operatorname{Infeasible}(j\prec i)\Longrightarrow i\prec j.
\]
Likewise, \(\operatorname{Infeasible}(i\prec j)\Longrightarrow j\prec i\). The inferred precedence may then tighten the successor's earliest start and the predecessor's latest completion.

Define \(\operatorname{First}(i,U)\) to mean \(i\prec j\) for every \(j\in U\setminus\{i\}\), and define \(\operatorname{Last}(i,U)\) analogously by \(j\prec i\). Not-first/not-last reasoning applies sound infeasibility tests to these hypotheses:
\[
\operatorname{Infeasible}(\operatorname{First}(i,U))\Longrightarrow\neg\operatorname{First}(i,U),
\qquad
\operatorname{Infeasible}(\operatorname{Last}(i,U))\Longrightarrow\neg\operatorname{Last}(i,U).

children.title: Capacity Profiles
children.top_down_role: Time-indexed views of available or consumed resource capacity.

assumptions_latex: Each cumulative activity \(i\in J\) has resource demand \(h_i\ge0\) and a compulsory interval \(K_i\).
The renewable resource has constant capacity \(C\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compulsory capacity profile is \(H(t)=\sum_{i\in J}h_i\mathbf 1_{K_i}(t)\), and feasibility requires \(H(t)\le C\) for every \(t\).

notation.meaning: compulsory resource load at time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: summing demands of mandatory execution intervals gives the compulsory cumulative profile
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compulsory-load profile for a constant-capacity cumulative resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given compulsory intervals \(K_i\), the capacity profile is the step function
\[
H(t)=\sum_{i\in J}h_i\mathbf 1_{K_i}(t).
\]
It records resource consumption forced by the current time bounds, independently of optional portions of activities. Since every feasible schedule executes each \(i\) throughout \(K_i\), cumulative feasibility implies
\[
H(t)\le C\qquad\text{for every }t.
\]
A profile value above \(C\) is therefore an immediate infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The capacity profile sums demands of all activities compelled to execute at each time; it must never exceed the cumulative resource capacity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and pointwise capacity condition are precise and fit the leaf, but no cumulative-scheduling citation is supplied.

children.title: Compulsory Parts
children.top_down_role: Mandatory temporal portions implied by current activity domains.

assumptions_latex: Activity \(i\) has processing time \(p_i>0\) and start domain \(s_i\in[\underline s_i,\overline s_i]\).
Execution is nonpreemptive on the half-open interval \([s_i,s_i+p_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compulsory part is \(K_i=[\overline s_i,\underline s_i+p_i)\) when \(\overline s_i<\underline s_i+p_i\), and is empty otherwise.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: intersection of all feasible execution intervals yields the displayed compulsory interval
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mandatory execution interval induced by an activity's current start bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The compulsory part of activity \(i\) is the intersection of its execution intervals over all currently allowed starts:
\[
K_i=\bigcap_{s_i\in[\underline s_i,\overline s_i]}[s_i,s_i+p_i)
=
\begin{cases}
[\overline s_i,\underline s_i+p_i),&\overline s_i<\underline s_i+p_i,\\
\varnothing,&\overline s_i\ge\underline s_i+p_i.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus every schedule respecting the current domain executes \(i\) throughout \(K_i\), while no other time point is forced solely by these bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An activity's compulsory part is the intersection of all execution intervals allowed by its current start bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_{-i}(t)\) be the compulsory capacity profile formed without activity \(i\). A candidate start \(s\) for \(i\) is inconsistent whenever
\[
\exists t\in[s,s+p_i)\quad H_{-i}(t)+h_i>C.
\]
Such a start would overlap a time at which compulsory demand from other activities leaves less than \(h_i\) residual capacity. Consequently, every interval of candidate starts whose executions intersect an offending profile segment may be removed from the domain of \(s_i\).

assumptions_latex: Each activity \(i\) has demand \(h_i\ge0\) and a compulsory interval \(K_i\).
The cumulative resource has capacity \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A time \(t^*\) with \(\sum_{i:t^*\in K_i}h_i>C\) certifies infeasibility of the current domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise infeasibility witness from compulsory cumulative demand.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose a time \(t^*\) and form the witness set \(W(t^*)=\{i:t^*\in K_i\}\). The pair
\[
\left(t^*,W(t^*)\right)
\]
is an overload certificate when
\[
\sum_{i\in W(t^*)}h_i>C.
\]
Membership \(t^*\in K_i\) verifies that every activity in the witness set must execute at \(t^*\) under every start allowed by its current domain. Their simultaneous mandatory demand therefore exceeds capacity, proving that the current cumulative-resource domains admit no feasible schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A witness time and its compulsory activities certify infeasibility when their mandatory demands sum to more than the resource capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Compulsory-Part Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-table propagation for nonpreemptive cumulative activities with fixed durations and demands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each activity \(i\), let \(s_i\in[\underline{s}_i,\overline{s}_i]\), duration \(p_i>0\), and demand \(h_i>0\). Its compulsory part is \(K_i=[\overline{s}_i,\underline{s}_i+p_i)\) when this interval is nonempty. Form the compulsory profile \(P(t)=\sum_{i:t\in K_i}h_i\). If \(P(t)>C\) at any time, report infeasibility. Otherwise, for each activity \(i\), delete every candidate start \(s\) for which some \(t\in[s,s+p_i)\) satisfies \(h_i+\sum_{j\ne i:t\in K_j}h_j>C\). Replace each start domain by the remaining values and repeat until no domain changes or a domain becomes empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build the mandatory resource profile, reject overloads, and remove any start time whose execution would exceed capacity together with other activities’ compulsory parts.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i\) has a finite integer or real interval domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Edge-Finding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Energetic edge-finding for one nonpreemptive cumulative resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given activities with current start domains, repeatedly examine an activity \(i\) and a nonempty set \(\Omega\) not containing it. For each candidate bound value \(v\), impose the corresponding edge hypothesis that \(i\) occupies the left or right boundary of the schedule region containing \(\Omega\). Compute a valid lower bound \(E(\Omega\cup\{i\},[a,b))\) on energy necessarily executed in every relevant interval \([a,b)\) under that hypothesis. If \(E(\Omega\cup\{i\},[a,b))>C(b-a)\), reject the hypothesis and tighten the implied lower or upper bound of \(s_i\). Iterate until no bound changes; report failure if a domain becomes empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test whether an activity can lie at either edge of a set’s scheduling region; an energetic overload under that hypothesis yields a sound start-bound update.
assumptions_latex: Each activity \(i\) is nonpreemptive with duration \(p_i>0\) and demand \(h_i>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Table Edge-Finding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid propagation combining compulsory profiles with cumulative edge-finding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct the compulsory profile \(P(t)\) from current activity bounds. For every tested interval \([a,b)\), reserve its compulsory load and define residual capacity energy \(R(a,b)=\int_a^b(C-P(t))\,dt\). For each activity set \(\Omega\) and edge candidate \(i\), compute a lower bound \(F(\Omega,i,[a,b))\) on noncompulsory energy forced into the interval by the corresponding left-edge or right-edge hypothesis. If \(F(\Omega,i,[a,b))>R(a,b)\), reject that hypothesis and tighten the appropriate bound of \(s_i\). Rebuild the profile after bound changes and iterate to a fixed point, failing when \(P(t)>C\) or a start domain is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge-finding is performed against capacity left after compulsory-profile load, yielding overload detection and stronger start-bound propagation.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive and have bounded starts, fixed durations, and fixed demands.
The resource has constant capacity \(C>0\).
The calculation of \(F\) excludes energy already counted in \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An edge hypothesis with \(F(\Omega,i,[a,b))>R(a,b)\) is impossible and supports the associated bound update.

knowledge_statements.title: Energy-Window Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Energetic infeasibility certificate for a fixed time window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For activities \(i\) with start domains \([\underline{s}_i,\overline{s}_i]\), define the least processing forced into \([a,b)\) by \(q_i(a,b)=\min_{s\in[\underline{s}_i,\overline{s}_i]}\lvert[s,s+p_i)\cap[a,b)\rvert\). The forced energy is \(E(a,b)=\sum_i h_iq_i(a,b)\). The tuple consisting of \([a,b)\), the current bounds, and the values \(q_i(a,b)\) is an overload certificate whenever \(E(a,b)>C(b-a)\). It is checked by independently minimizing each interval intersection and comparing the resulting demand-time sum with the total resource energy available in the window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A window is infeasible when activities must consume more demand-time inside it than the resource can supply there.
