knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise nonoverlap with boundary contact permitted by the half-open-box convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nonoverlap constraint requires \(O_i(x_i)\cap O_j(x_j)=\varnothing\) for all distinct \(i,j\). Equivalently, for every component pair \(B_{ik}(x_i)\), \(B_{jh}(x_j)\), at least one coordinate \(r\) separates them: \[x_{i,r}+u_{ik,r}\le x_{j,r}+\ell_{jh,r}\quad\text{or}\quad x_{j,r}+u_{jh,r}\le x_{i,r}+\ell_{ik,r}.\] The separating coordinate may depend on the object pair and component pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every pair of component boxes from distinct objects must be separated along at least one coordinate, while boundary contact is allowed.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonoverlap Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise component-box separation condition is mathematically coherent under the half-open convention and fits the leaf, but it has no supporting citation.

children.title: Containment–Nonoverlap Interaction
children.top_down_role: Coupling between placement boundaries and pairwise exclusion.

assumptions_latex: For each object \(i\), let \(F_i=\{x:O_i(x)\subseteq C\}\) be its containment-feasible origin set.
For fixed \(x_j\), let \(D_{ij}(x_j)=\{x:O_i(x)\cap O_j(x_j)\ne\varnothing\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i\in F_i\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}D_{ij}(x_j)\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: Origins of object i causing overlap with fixed object j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasible-origin representation of coupled containment and nonoverlap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-origin representation of containment and pairwise nonoverlap coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A placement \((x_i)_i\) satisfies the coupled containment-nonoverlap system exactly when, for every object \(i\), \[x_i\in F_i\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}D_{ij}(x_j).\] Containment first restricts \(x_i\) to \(F_i\); each fixed placement \(x_j\) then removes the forbidden-origin region \(D_{ij}(x_j)\). Consequently, either restriction may strengthen propagation of the other by shrinking the remaining feasible origin set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An object's feasible origins are its containment-feasible origins minus all origins that overlap another placed object.
knowledge_statements.title: Containment–Nonoverlap Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-origin representation matches the interaction leaf, but its Geost interpretation and propagation claim lack an inspectable authoritative source.

assumptions_latex: For every object \(i\), \(O_i(x_i)\subseteq B_i(x_i)\), where \(B_i(x_i)\) is an axis-aligned bounding box.
The container \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is arbitrary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_i(x_i)\cap B_j(x_j)=\varnothing\Rightarrow O_i(x_i)\cap O_j(x_j)=\varnothing\), and \(B_i(x_i)\subseteq C\Rightarrow O_i(x_i)\subseteq C\).

notation.meaning: Exact occupied region of object i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary set-inclusion implications underlying bounding-box filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound but generally incomplete inference using enclosing axis-aligned boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(O_i(x_i)\subseteq B_i(x_i)\), disjoint bounding boxes certify nonoverlap: \[B_i(x_i)\cap B_j(x_j)=\varnothing\Longrightarrow O_i(x_i)\cap O_j(x_j)=\varnothing.\] Likewise, \(B_i(x_i)\subseteq C\) certifies containment of \(O_i(x_i)\). The converses generally fail for nonrectangular or disconnected shapes: occupied regions can be disjoint even when their bounding boxes overlap, and a shape can lie in a non-box container while its bounding box does not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjoint enclosing boxes certify object nonoverlap, and a contained enclosing box certifies object containment; neither converse holds for general shapes.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Bounding-Box Reasoning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounding-box implications are sound and the property kind fits, but no source supports their placement in the Geost reasoning context.

children.title: Geometric Symmetry
children.top_down_role: Equivalent geometric placements induced by transformations or interchangeable objects.

assumptions_latex: Let \(X\) be the set of complete geometric placements and \(F\subseteq X\) its feasible subset.
A group \(G\) acts on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(gF=F\) for every \(g\in G\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: group-action definition of symmetry for a feasible geometric model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Group-action symmetry of a geometric feasibility or optimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A geometric symmetry is an element \(g\in G\) such that feasibility is invariant under its action: \[x\in F\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad gx\in F.\] The group may act by permuting indistinguishable objects, transforming coordinates while preserving the container and shapes, or combining both actions. For an optimization model with objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), an objective-preserving symmetry additionally satisfies \(f(gx)=f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A geometric symmetry is a group action that maps feasible placements to feasible placements and, when relevant, preserves objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Symmetry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The group-action formulation is plausible, but an authoritative source is needed to establish the intended Geost-specific meaning and whether the leaf denotes individual symmetries or an invariant symmetry group.

children.title: Geometric Dominance
children.top_down_role: Placement comparisons that identify structurally inferior alternatives.

assumptions_latex: Let \(P\) be a set of partial placements, with completion set \(\operatorname{Ext}(p)\subseteq F\) for each \(p\in P\).
Let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\) be minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\succeq q\Longleftrightarrow(\forall z\in\operatorname{Ext}(q))(\exists y\in\operatorname{Ext}(p))\ f(y)\le f(z)\).

notation.meaning: Feasible completions extending partial placement p.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: completion-based dominance definition for minimization search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion-based dominance for partial placements in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial placement \(p\) dominates a partial placement \(q\), written \(p\succeq q\), when \[\bigl(\forall z\in\operatorname{Ext}(q)\bigr)\bigl(\exists y\in\operatorname{Ext}(p)\bigr)\ f(y)\le f(z).\] Thus every feasible completion available below \(q\) has a completion below \(p\) that is at least as good. In a feasibility problem, omit \(f\) and require that \(\operatorname{Ext}(q)\ne\varnothing\) implies \(\operatorname{Ext}(p)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial placement dominates another when every completion of the latter can be matched by an equally good or better completion of the former.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Dominance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The completion-based minimization relation is internally precise, but geometric dominance has multiple formulations; no citation establishes that this is the intended variant for the leaf.

children.title: Symmetry–Dominance Interaction
children.top_down_role: Cases where geometric equivalence affects dominance comparisons.

assumptions_latex: A group \(G\) acts on partial placements and preserves feasibility and objective values of their completions.
Dominance \(\succeq\) has the completion-based meaning stated for geometric dominance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\succeq gq\Rightarrow gq\) may be discarded without changing the optimal value.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orbit reduction combined with completion-preserving dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe pruning obtained by applying dominance across symmetry orbits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any partial placement \(q\), its orbit is \(Gq=\{gq:g\in G\}\). If a retained partial placement \(p\) satisfies \(p\succeq gq\) for some \(g\in G\), then the search branch rooted at \(gq\) may be discarded: every completion lost there has an equally good or better completion below \(p\). In particular, selecting one undominated canonical representative from each orbit preserves feasibility and the optimal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetry-equivalent branch may be pruned when a retained partial placement dominates it; undominated orbit representatives suffice for optimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry–Dominance Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symmetry-orbit dominance principle fits the interaction leaf, but the safe-pruning and representative-selection claims require a source stating the relevant hypotheses.

children.title: Structured Data Aggregation-Ordering Globals
children.top_down_role: Set relations, array access, channeling, arithmetic aggregation, sorting, lexicographic order, and symmetry-oriented ordering.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Set-related, array-related, mathematical, channeling, sorting, and lexicographic constraints

assumptions_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite index set and let \(S_i\subseteq U\) be set variables over a common finite universe \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_i\cap S_j=\varnothing\) for all distinct \(i,j\in I\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard pairwise-disjoint set global constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise disjointness of finite set variables over a common universe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set-disjointness constraint on \((S_i)_{i\in I}\) holds exactly when \[\forall i,j\in I,\,i\ne j:\quad S_i\cap S_j=\varnothing.\] Equivalently, each element of \(U\) belongs to at most one indexed set: \[\forall u\in U:\quad \sum_{i\in I}\mathbf{1}[u\in S_i]\le 1.\] Empty sets are permitted unless excluded by separate cardinality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indexed set variables are pairwise disjoint, equivalently each universe element occurs in at most one set.
knowledge_statements.title: Set Disjointness Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly expresses pairwise disjointness and its finite-universe indicator form, but no constraint-catalogue citation is supplied.

assumptions_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite nonempty index set and let \(S_i\subseteq U\) be set variables over a finite universe \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcup_{i\in I}S_i=U\) and \(S_i\cap S_j=\varnothing\) whenever \(i\ne j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Labeled finite partition; empty blocks are allowed unless separately forbidden.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set-partition constraint holds exactly when the indexed sets cover \(U\) without duplication: \[\bigcup_{i\in I}S_i=U\quad\text{and}\quad \forall i\ne j:\ S_i\cap S_j=\varnothing.\] Equivalently, every \(u\in U\) has exactly one containing block, \[\forall u\in U:\quad \sum_{i\in I}\mathbf{1}[u\in S_i]=1.\] This definition labels blocks by \(I\) and permits empty blocks unless nonemptiness is imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sets form labeled blocks covering the universe exactly once; empty blocks remain possible unless separately prohibited.
knowledge_statements.title: Set Partition Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The labeled cover-and-disjointness condition is precise, including its empty-block convention, but that convention and the global-constraint semantics are uncited.

assumptions_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite index set, let \(X_i\) be finite-domain variables taking values in \(V\), and let \(S\subseteq I\), \(T\subseteq V\) be set variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\{i\in I:X_i\in T\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-domain ROOTS constraint relating selected indices to selected values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraint \(\operatorname{ROOTS}((X_i)_{i\in I},S,T)\) holds exactly when \[S=\{i\in I:X_i\in T\}.\] Equivalently, for every index \(i\in I\), \[i\in S\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X_i\in T.\] Both implications are part of the global constraint: membership of \(i\) in \(S\) forces \(X_i\) into \(T\), while exclusion of \(i\) forces \(X_i\) outside \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ROOTS makes the set variable contain exactly those indices whose corresponding integer-variable values belong to a designated value set.
knowledge_statements.title: Roots Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bidirectional ROOTS semantics are standard and fit the leaf, but no authoritative catalogue or paper with a specific locator is cited.

assumptions_latex: Let \(I,J\) be finite index sets, let \(X_i\) be integer variables with \(X_i\in J\), and let \(S_j\subseteq I\) be set variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_i=j\Longleftrightarrow i\in S_j\) for every \((i,j)\in I\times J\).

notation.meaning: Integer variable assigning index i to a label in J.
Set of indices assigned label j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Channeling between integer labels and their set-valued inverse images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Integer-set channeling holds exactly when \[\forall i\in I,\ \forall j\in J:\quad X_i=j\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad i\in S_j.\] Hence \(S_j=\{i\in I:X_i=j\}\) for every \(j\in J\). Because every \(X_i\) takes exactly one value in \(J\), the family \((S_j)_{j\in J}\) forms a partition of \(I\), with empty sets allowed for unused labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each set contains exactly the indices whose integer variables equal its label; consequently, the sets partition the integer-variable indices.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer–Set Channeling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integer–set inverse-image channel is mathematically precise and implies the stated partition, but the selected channeling convention has no supporting citation.

assumptions_latex: Let \(U\) be finite, let \(S\subseteq U\) be a set variable, and let \(b_u\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_u=1\Longleftrightarrow u\in S\) for every \(u\in U\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: characteristic-vector representation of a finite set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bidirectional channeling between a finite set and its Boolean characteristic vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set-Boolean channeling imposes, for every \(u\in U\), \[b_u=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u\in S,\qquad b_u=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u\notin S.\] Thus the Boolean vector \((b_u)_{u\in U}\) is exactly the characteristic vector of \(S\), and \[S=\{u\in U:b_u=1\},\qquad |S|=\sum_{u\in U}b_u.\] The equivalences provide propagation in both directions between set membership and Boolean assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each Boolean is one exactly when its universe element belongs to the set, giving the set's characteristic-vector representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Set–Boolean Channeling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The characteristic-vector representation and cardinality identity are correct for finite sets and fit the leaf, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Set Channeling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain channeling between an integer array and its inverse family of index sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) and \(V\) be finite sets, let \(x=(x_i)_{i\in I}\) satisfy \(x_i\in V\), and let \((S_v)_{v\in V}\) be set variables with \(S_v\subseteq I\). The inverse-set channeling constraint is
\[
\forall i\in I\;\forall v\in V:\quad i\in S_v\ \Longleftrightarrow\ x_i=v.
\]
Consequently, the sets \((S_v)_{v\in V}\) form a partition of \(I\), empty parts being permitted, and each set is exactly the inverse image \(S_v=x^{-1}(\{v\})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each set variable contains exactly the indices whose corresponding integer variable takes its associated value; these inverse-image sets partition the index set.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(V\) are finite.
\(x_i\in V\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in S_v\Longleftrightarrow x_i=v\), and \((S_v)_{v\in V}\) partitions \(I\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not specifically support inverse-set channeling, its biconditional semantics, or the partition conclusion. A source on inverse/channeling constraints with a precise definition locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Element Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional finite-array element constraint with a variable index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be a finite index set, let \(a=(a_j)_{j\in D}\) be an array of constants or variables over a common value set \(U\), and let \(i\in D\) and \(y\in U\) be variables. The element constraint \(\operatorname{element}(i,a,y)\) holds exactly when
\[
y=a_i.
\]
Thus every satisfying assignment selects the array entry at the realized index, and the selected entry and \(y\) must take the same value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An element constraint equates an output variable with the array entry selected by a variable index.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and nonempty.
\(i\in D\).
All \(a_j\) and \(y\) share value set \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{element}(i,a,y)\Longleftrightarrow y=a_i\).

notation.meaning: indexed array of constants or variables

knowledge_statements.title: Membership Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Membership in the collection of values occurring in a finite array.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be a finite nonempty index set, let \(a=(a_j)_{j\in D}\) be an array with entries in a value set \(U\), and let \(y\in U\). The array-membership constraint \(\operatorname{member}(y,a)\) holds exactly when
\[
\exists j\in D:\quad y=a_j.
\]
For a reified Boolean variable \(b\in\{0,1\}\), the reified form is \(b=1\Longleftrightarrow\exists j\in D:\ y=a_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The membership constraint requires a value to equal at least one entry of a finite array; its reified form records this truth value.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and nonempty.
\(a_j,y\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{member}(y,a)\Longleftrightarrow \exists j\in D:\ y=a_j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Indexed Array Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A family of element constraints representing reads through variable indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) and \(K\) be finite sets, let \(a=(a_j)_{j\in D}\) be an array over \(U\), and let \((i_k)_{k\in K}\) satisfy \(i_k\in D\). The variable-indexed view \(v=(v_k)_{k\in K}\) of \(a\) through \(i\) is represented by
\[
\forall k\in K:\quad v_k=a_{i_k}.
\]
Equivalently, it is the conjunction \(\bigwedge_{k\in K}\operatorname{element}(i_k,a,v_k)\); repeated indices therefore induce equal view components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-indexed view consists of outputs obtained by reading one array through several variable indices; it is a conjunction of element constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) and \(K\) are finite.
\(i_k\in D\) for every \(k\in K\).
Array and view entries lie in \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_k=a_{i_k}\) for every \(k\in K\).

notation.meaning: index used by view component k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically reasonable and its content kind fits, but the cited general CP section does not specifically support the introduced notion of a variable-indexed array view, its conjunction representation, or the repeated-index consequence. A direct array/view or element-constraint source is required.

children.title: Array Write Constraints
children.top_down_role: Array-update constraints representing a single indexed write.

knowledge_statements.title: Array Write Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional single-cell update of a finite array.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be a finite index set, let \(a=(a_j)_{j\in D}\) be an input array over \(U\), let \(i\in D\), let \(x\in U\), and let \(b=(b_j)_{j\in D}\) be an output array. The array-write constraint \(b=\operatorname{write}(a,i,x)\) holds exactly when
\[
\forall j\in D:\quad b_j=\begin{cases}x,&j=i,\\a_j,&j\ne i.\end{cases}
\]
Hence the selected cell receives \(x\), while every other cell is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An array write replaces the entry at one variable index with a supplied value and preserves all other entries.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and nonempty.
\(i\in D\).
The arrays and written value range over \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_i=x\) and \(b_j=a_j\) for every \(j\ne i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The functional update definition is precise and locally appropriate, but the cited general CP section does not specifically support array-write constraints or their frame semantics. A source defining array update/write with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Sequential-Write Constraints
children.top_down_role: Array-update constraints representing ordered sequences of writes.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential-Write Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered composition of single-cell functional array updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) and \(T=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be finite, let \(a^{0}\) be an array over \(U\), and for each \(t\in T\) let \(i_t\in D\) and \(x_t\in U\). Sequential writes are represented by intermediate arrays satisfying
\[
a^{t}=\operatorname{write}(a^{t-1},i_t,x_t)\qquad(t=1,\ldots,m).
\]
The output is \(a^{m}\). For every cell, its output is the value of the latest write to that cell, or its initial value when no write targets it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential writes compose single-cell updates in their specified order, with intermediate arrays exposing each state and the final array as output.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and nonempty.
\(i_t\in D\) and \(x_t\in U\) for \(t=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{m}=\operatorname{write}(\cdots\operatorname{write}(a^{0},i_1,x_1)\cdots,i_m,x_m)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordered-composition representation is plausible, but the citation does not specifically support sequential array writes. In addition, the domain of m is not stated; a corrected sourced version should declare m as a nonnegative integer and handle the m=0 case explicitly.

children.title: Write-Order Semantics
children.top_down_role: Effects of write ordering on resulting array views.

knowledge_statements.title: Write-Order Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Last-write-wins semantics for an explicitly ordered finite update sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under sequential-write semantics, fix a cell \(j\in D\) and define \(T_j=\{t\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:i_t=j\}\). Then the final array satisfies
\[
a_j^{m}=\begin{cases}a_j^{0},&T_j=\varnothing,\\x_{\max T_j},&T_j\ne\varnothing.\end{cases}
\]
Thus writes to distinct cells commute, whereas two writes to the same cell commute only when their written values agree; otherwise reversing their order changes that cell's final value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The last update targeting a cell determines its final value; updates to different cells commute, but conflicting updates to one cell generally do not.
assumptions_latex: Writes are applied in the total order \(1,\ldots,m\).
Each update has semantics \(a^t=\operatorname{write}(a^{t-1},i_t,x_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_j^m=a_j^0\) if \(T_j=\varnothing\), and \(a_j^m=x_{\max T_j}\) otherwise.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The last-write-wins formula and content kind fit the leaf, but D, m, the write sequence, the arrays, and the value domain are not introduced within the record. The cited general CP section also does not specifically support these write-order semantics. A direct source and a self-contained restatement are required.

children.title: Sum Constraints
children.top_down_role: Additive aggregation over collections of decision expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Sum Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite unweighted linear aggregation with equality or inequality comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, let \((x_i)_{i\in I}\) be numerical variables, let \(y\) be a numerical variable or constant, and let \(\bowtie\in\{=,\le,\ge\}\). The sum constraint \(\operatorname{sum}(x,\bowtie,y)\) is the relation
\[
\sum_{i\in I}x_i\ \bowtie\ y.
\]
The empty-sum convention is \(\sum_{i\in\varnothing}x_i=0\). Domains must be chosen in a common ordered additive structure in which the displayed finite sum and comparison are defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum constraint compares the unweighted finite sum of its input variables with a target using equality or an order relation.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
Inputs and target belong to a common ordered additive domain.
\(\bowtie\in\{=,\le,\ge\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{sum}(x,\bowtie,y)\Longleftrightarrow \sum_{i\in I}x_i\bowtie y\).

children.title: Scalar-Product Constraints
children.top_down_role: Coefficient-weighted additive aggregation over decision expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar-Product Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite weighted linear aggregation with fixed coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, let \((a_i)_{i\in I}\) be fixed scalars, let \((x_i)_{i\in I}\) be numerical variables, let \(y\) be a numerical variable or constant, and let \(\bowtie\in\{=,\le,\ge\}\). The scalar-product constraint is
\[
\operatorname{scalar\_product}(a,x,\bowtie,y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sum_{i\in I}a_i x_i\ \bowtie\ y.
\]
All products, sums, and comparisons are interpreted in a common ordered scalar domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar-product constraint compares a fixed-coefficient weighted sum of variables with a target.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
The coefficients \(a_i\) are fixed.
Products, sums, and \(\bowtie\) are defined in a common ordered scalar domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{scalar\_product}(a,x,\bowtie,y)\Longleftrightarrow \sum_{i\in I}a_i x_i\bowtie y\).

children.title: Coefficient-Regime Specialization
children.top_down_role: Structural distinctions arising from coefficient patterns in additive aggregates.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Regime Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical reductions of scalar products under uniform, binary, and signed-unit coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the scalar-product relation \(\sum_{i\in I}a_i x_i\bowtie y\), particular coefficient regimes give exact specializations. If \(a_i=1\) for all \(i\), it is the sum constraint \(\sum_i x_i\bowtie y\). If \(a_i\in\{0,1\}\), it is \(\sum_{i:a_i=1}x_i\bowtie y\). If \(a_i\in\{-1,0,1\}\), it is
\[
\sum_{i:a_i=1}x_i-\sum_{i:a_i=-1}x_i\ \bowtie\ y.
\]
Each transformation preserves exactly the satisfying assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform, binary, and signed-unit coefficient vectors reduce a scalar product respectively to a sum, subset sum, or difference of two sums.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
Coefficients are fixed and belong to the stated regime.
All displayed operations and comparisons are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The specialized sum expression is equal to \(\sum_{i\in I}a_i x_i\) and therefore defines the same constraint.

children.title: Minimum Constraints
children.top_down_role: Aggregation constraints selecting or representing the least value.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nonempty minimum aggregation over a totally ordered value domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite and nonempty, let \((x_i)_{i\in I}\) and \(m\) take values in a totally ordered set. The minimum constraint \(\operatorname{minimum}(m,x)\) holds exactly when
\[
m=\min_{i\in I}x_i.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\bigl(\forall i\in I:\ m\le x_i\bigr)\ \land\ \bigl(\exists k\in I:\ m=x_k\bigr).
\]
The witness condition distinguishes an attained finite minimum from a mere lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum constraint makes its result equal to an attained least value among a finite nonempty family of variables.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and nonempty.
All \(x_i\) and \(m\) lie in one totally ordered set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m=\min_{i\in I}x_i\).

children.title: Maximum Constraints
children.top_down_role: Aggregation constraints selecting or representing the greatest value.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nonempty maximum aggregation over a totally ordered value domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite and nonempty, let \((x_i)_{i\in I}\) and \(M\) take values in a totally ordered set. The maximum constraint \(\operatorname{maximum}(M,x)\) holds exactly when
\[
M=\max_{i\in I}x_i.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\bigl(\forall i\in I:\ M\ge x_i\bigr)\ \land\ \bigl(\exists k\in I:\ M=x_k\bigr).
\]
The witness condition distinguishes an attained finite maximum from a mere upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximum constraint makes its result equal to an attained greatest value among a finite nonempty family of variables.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and nonempty.
All \(x_i\) and \(M\) lie in one totally ordered set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M=\max_{i\in I}x_i\).

children.title: Extremum Duality
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between lower-extreme and upper-extreme formulations.

assumptions_latex: Let \(n\ge 1\) and \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_i x_i=-\max_i(-x_i)\) and \(\max_i x_i=-\min_i(-x_i)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary order reversal under negation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scalar extremum constraints over a nonempty indexed family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every nonempty finite vector \(x\), negation reverses its order, so
\[
\min_{1\le i\le n}x_i=-\max_{1\le i\le n}(-x_i),\qquad
\max_{1\le i\le n}x_i=-\min_{1\le i\le n}(-x_i).
\]
Consequently, the constraint \(m=\min_i x_i\) is equivalent to \(-m=\max_i(-x_i)\), and \(M=\max_i x_i\) is equivalent to \(-M=\min_i(-x_i)\). The equivalences preserve all ties among extremizing indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating every entry exchanges minimum and maximum, while preserving which indices attain the extremum.
knowledge_statements.title: Extremum Duality

k\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{1\le i\le n}x_i
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x_k=	au\ \text{ and }\ \tau\le x_i\ \text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,n\},

where \(\tau=\min_i x_i\). Equivalently, it is the conjunction \(x_k\le x_i\) for all \(i\). If several components equal \(\tau\), every corresponding index is admissible unless an additional tie-breaking constraint is specified.

assumptions_latex: Let \(n\ge 1\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and \(v\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v=x_k=\min_i x_i\) or \(v=x_k=\max_i x_i\), according to the selected extremum mode.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact value-index channeling for finite minimum or maximum constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Minimum-index channeling is the joint constraint
\[
v=x_k,\qquad v\le x_i\quad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,n\};
\]
maximum-index channeling replaces the inequalities by \(v\ge x_i\) for every \(i\). Thus \(k\) identifies a component, \(v\) equals that component, and the universal inequalities certify its extremality. Conversely, any pair \((k,v)\) satisfying the appropriate system has \(k\) in the corresponding arg-extremum set and \(v\) equal to the extremum value.

children.title: Tied-Extremum Regimes

assumptions_latex: Let \(n\ge 1\) and \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_{\min}(x)=\{i:x_i=\min_jx_j\}\) and \(I_{\max}(x)=\{i:x_i=\max_jx_j\}\); ties occur exactly when the relevant set has size greater than one.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tie semantics for finite arg-extremum constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
I_{\min}(x)=\{i:x_i=\min_jx_j\},\qquad
I_{\max}(x)=\{i:x_i=\max_jx_j\}.
\]
A minimum tie occurs exactly when \(|I_{\min}(x)|>1\), and a maximum tie occurs exactly when \(|I_{\max}(x)|>1\). Under set-valued arg-extremum semantics, any member of the relevant set is feasible. A deterministic first-index regime adds \(k=\min I_{\min}(x)\) or \(k=\min I_{\max}(x)\); a last-index regime analogously uses the largest member.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ties are represented by the full set of extremizing indices; optional first- or last-index rules turn this relation into a unique choice.

Piecewise-Linear Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable finite piecewise-affine aggregation with explicit region selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(D_i=\bigcup_{r=1}^{q_i}P_{ir}\) and \(f_i(u)=a_{ir}^{\mathsf T}u+b_{ir}\) for \(u\in P_{ir}\), with consistent values on overlapping boundaries. The aggregation constraint is
\[
y=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i).
\]
Equivalently, for every \(i\), select at least one region \(r_i\) containing \(x_i\), impose \(z_i=a_{ir_i}^{\mathsf T}x_i+b_{ir_i}\), and impose \(y=\sum_{i=1}^n z_i\). If the regions are disjoint, the selected piece is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A piecewise-linear aggregate sums local affine expressions, selecting at least one valid region for each argument; selection is unique when the regions are disjoint.
assumptions_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), let \(f_i:D_i\to\mathbb{R}\) be piecewise affine on a finite polyhedral partition of \(D_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\).

assumptions_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) and \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)\) take values in a totally ordered set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_1\le\cdots\le y_n\) and \(y\) is a permutation of \(x\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondecreasing sorting of a finite sequence over a total order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The sorting constraint \(\operatorname{sort}(x,y)\) holds if and only if
\[
y_1\le y_2\le\cdots\le y_n
\quad\text{and}\quad
\exists\pi\in S_n\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:\ y_i=x_{\pi(i)}.
\]
Equivalently, \(x\) and \(y\) have the same value multiplicities and \(y\) is nondecreasing. Because the ambient order is total, the value sequence \(y\) is uniquely determined by \(x\), although permutations witnessing the equality need not be unique when values repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sorting constraint makes the output nondecreasing while preserving exactly the multiset of input values.
knowledge_statements.title: Sorting Constraints

assumptions_latex: Let \(m,n\ge1\), and let \(u^1,\ldots,u^m\) be length-\(n\) vectors over a totally ordered set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u^1\le_{\mathrm{lex}}u^2\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\le_{\mathrm{lex}}u^m\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-strict lexicographic chain over equal-length finite vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For equal-length vectors \(a,b\), define \(a\le_{\mathrm{lex}}b\) when either \(a=b\), or there exists \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) such that \(a_i=b_i\) for every \(i<j\) and \(a_j<b_j\). The lexicographic chain constraint is
\[
\bigwedge_{r=1}^{m-1}u^r\le_{\mathrm{lex}}u^{r+1}.
\]
By transitivity, it also implies \(u^r\le_{\mathrm{lex}}u^s\) for every \(r<s\). Replacing each non-strict comparison by a strict one defines the strict-chain variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lexicographic chain requires every vector to precede its successor at the first coordinate where they differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Chain Constraints

assumptions_latex: Let \(X\in D^{m\times n}\), where \(D\) is totally ordered, and fix the natural top-to-bottom and left-to-right coordinate orders.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_{\bullet,1}\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\le_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\bullet,n}\), optionally together with \(X_{1,\bullet}\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\le_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{m,\bullet}\).

notation.meaning: Lexicographic order induced by the fixed coordinate order.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-orientation row and column lexicographic ordering for finite matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Column lexicographic ordering imposes
\[
X_{\bullet,1}\le_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\bullet,2}\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\le_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\bullet,n},
\]
where columns are read from row \(1\) through row \(m\). The row analogue imposes \(X_{1,\bullet}\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\le_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{m,\bullet}\), reading each row from column \(1\) through column \(n\). A double-lex constraint is the conjunction of both chains. The chosen increasing or decreasing orientation must remain fixed throughout the constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix lexicographic ordering arranges consecutive columns, rows, or both using a fixed lexicographic orientation.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Lexicographic Ordering

assumptions_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) take values in a finite set \(V\), and let \(v_1\prec v_2\prec\cdots\prec v_q\) be designated values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{first}_x(v_1)<\cdots<\operatorname{first}_x(v_q)\) for the values that occur, with occurrence of \(v_j\) implying occurrence of every predecessor.

notation.meaning: First position containing \(v\), or \(+\infty\) if absent.
Required precedence order on designated values.

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-occurrence precedence with absent values placed after all positions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(\operatorname{first}_x(v)=\min\{i:x_i=v\}\) when \(v\) occurs and \(\operatorname{first}_x(v)=+\infty\) otherwise. The value-precedence constraint for \(v_1\prec\cdots\prec v_q\) holds when, for all \(1\le r<s\le q\),
\[
\operatorname{first}_x(v_s)<+\infty
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{first}_x(v_r)<\operatorname{first}_x(v_s).
\]
Thus a later designated value cannot appear before the first occurrence of each required predecessor, and cannot appear at all when a predecessor is absent.

assumptions_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\) be invariant under all column permutations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The canonical-representative set for the column-permutation action on \(F\) is
\[
F^{\downarrow}=\{X\in F:X_{\bullet,1}\ge_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\ge_{\mathrm{lex}}X_{\bullet,n}\}.

Its orbitope interface is the polytope \(\mathcal O(F)=\operatorname{conv}(F^{\downarrow})\). C\cap Gx\ne\varnothing\qquad\text{for every }x\in F,

knowledge_statements.title: Orbitope–Permutation Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary assignment matrices under column-permutation symmetry, represented by the partitioning orbitope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_{p,q}=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{p\times q}:\sum_{j=1}^{q}x_{ij}=1\text{ for every }i\}\), and let \(S_q\) act on \(X_{p,q}\) by permuting columns. knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Based Violation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hamming-distance softening of a finite-domain constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) be a nonempty constraint relation and let \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\). The variable-based violation of \(C\) at \(a\) is \[\operatorname{viol}_{\mathrm{var}}(a,C)=\min_{b\in C}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf{1}[a_i\ne b_i].\] Thus it is the minimum number of variable assignments that must be changed to obtain a tuple satisfying \(C\); it equals zero exactly when \(a\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-based violation is the minimum number of assigned variables whose values must change to produce a satisfying tuple.
assumptions_latex: Each \(D_i\) is a finite nonempty domain.
\(C\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Based Violation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Violation measured by unsatisfied members of a specified constraint decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a constraint be presented as \(C=\bigcap_{j=1}^{m}C_j\) on a common tuple space \(D\), and assign nonnegative weights \(w_j\) to its component constraints. For \(a\in D\), define \[\operatorname{viol}_{\mathrm{con}}(a;C_1,\ldots,C_m)=\sum_{j=1}^{m}w_j\mathbf{1}[a\notin C_j].\] With unit weights this counts violated component constraints. The measure depends on the declared decomposition, not merely on the relation \(C\), and it is zero exactly when every positive-weight component is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-based violation sums the weights of violated constraints in a declared decomposition of the global constraint.

\(w_j\ge 0\) for every \(j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Value-Based Violation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality deviation measured separately for each value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in V^n\), and prescribe lower and upper occurrence bounds \(\ell_v,u_v\) for every \(v\in V\). Write \(N_v(a)=|\{i:a_i=v\}|\). The value-based violation is \[\operatorname{viol}_{\mathrm{val}}(a)=\sum_{v\in V}\bigl(\max\{0,\ell_v-N_v(a)\}+\max\{0,N_v(a)-u_v\}\bigr).\] It aggregates deficits and excesses by value and is zero exactly when every value count lies within its prescribed interval.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost string editing into the language accepted by a sequence constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma\) be a finite alphabet, let \(L\subseteq\Sigma^*\) be the language of valid sequences, and give insertion, deletion, and substitution operations nonnegative costs. For \(x\in\Sigma^*\), define \[\operatorname{viol}_{\mathrm{edit}}(x,L)=\inf_{y\in L}d_{\mathrm{edit}}(x,y),\] where \(d_{\mathrm{edit}}(x,y)\) is the minimum total cost of an edit script transforming \(x\) into \(y\). knowledge_statements.title: Soft AllDifferent Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-based softening of AllDifferent by duplicate occurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a tuple \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in V^n\), let \(N_v(a)=|\{i:a_i=v\}|\). The value-based soft AllDifferent constraint introduces a cost variable \(z\) satisfying \[z=\sum_{v\in V}\max\{0,N_v(a)-1\}=n-|\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}|.\] Hence \(z\) counts occurrences beyond the first occurrence of each used value. The hard AllDifferent constraint is recovered by imposing \(z=0\); an optimization model may instead minimize or bound \(z\).

knowledge_statements.title: Soft Global Cardinality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soft global cardinality through weighted lower-bound deficits and upper-bound excesses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\in V^n\), with occurrence bounds \(0\le\ell_v\le u_v\le n\) and nonnegative deficit and excess weights \(c_v^-,c_v^+\). A soft global cardinality constraint introduces \(z\) such that \[z=\sum_{v\in V}\left(c_v^-\max\{0,\ell_v-N_v(a)\}+c_v^+\max\{0,N_v(a)-u_v\}\right),\] where \(N_v(a)=|\{i:a_i=v\}|\). If every weight is positive, \(z=0\) exactly when the hard global cardinality bounds hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A soft global cardinality constraint penalizes weighted deficits and excesses in each value's occurrence count.

children.title: Shared Cardinality-Violation Structure

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Cardinality-Violation Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: AllDifferent represented as a special global cardinality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a\in V^n\), impose global-cardinality bounds \(\ell_v=0\) and \(u_v=1\) for every \(v\in V\). The resulting hard global cardinality constraint is exactly AllDifferent. Moreover, its unit-weight excess violation is \[\sum_{v\in V}\max\{0,N_v(a)-1\}=n-|\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}|.\] Thus value-based SoftAllDifferent is the upper-excess specialization of SoftGCC, with no lower-bound deficit terms.

children.title: Soft Regular Constraints
children.top_down_role: Costed acceptance variants for sequences represented through finite-state structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Soft Regular Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-length soft regular constraint represented by a weighted layered automaton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\) be a deterministic finite automaton and let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\Sigma^n\). Form a layered graph with states \((i,q)\) for \(0\le i\le n\). For each chosen symbol \(x_i\), arcs from \((i-1,q)\) to \((i,\delta(q,a))\) carry a prescribed nonnegative mismatch cost \(c_i(x_i,a)\). The soft Regular cost is the minimum path cost from \((0,q_0)\) to some \((n,f)\), \(f\in F\). With zero cost only for matching symbols, cost zero is equivalent to acceptance of \(x\) by \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft Regular is the cheapest accepting path through a layered automaton when symbol mismatches carry nonnegative costs.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a deterministic finite automaton and \(x\in\Sigma^n\).
\(c_i(b,a)\ge0\), with \(c_i(b,a)=0\iff a=b\).

children.title: Soft Sequence Constraints
children.top_down_role: Penalized sequence-window, occurrence, and pattern restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Soft Sequence Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Window-count Sequence constraint softened by additive deficit and excess penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in D^n\), choose \(S\subseteq D\), a window length \(k\), and bounds \(0\le\ell\le u\le k\). For each window start \(t\), define \(W_t(x)=\sum_{i=t}^{t+k-1}\mathbf{1}[x_i\in S]\). The additive soft Sequence cost is \[z=\sum_{t=1}^{n-k+1}\left(c_t^-\max\{0,\ell-W_t(x)\}+c_t^+\max\{0,W_t(x)-u\}\right).\] With positive weights, \(z=0\) exactly when every length-\(k\) window satisfies the hard Sequence bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft Sequence sums weighted lower-bound deficits and upper-bound excesses across all fixed-length windows.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite, \(x\in D^n\), and \(1\le k\le n\).
\(0\le\ell\le u\le k\) and \(c_t^-,c_t^+>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z=0\iff \ell\le W_t(x)\le u\) for every \(t=1,\ldots,n-k+1\).

children.title: Automaton-Based Violation Costs
children.top_down_role: State-transition cost structures shared by regular-language and sequence-pattern softening.

knowledge_statements.title: Automaton-Based Violation Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic programming for minimum-cost acceptance of an assigned sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a deterministic finite automaton \(A=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\), a sequence \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\Sigma^n\), and nonnegative transition-use costs \(c_i(x_i,a)\). Initialize \(d_0(q_0)=0\) and \(d_0(q)=+\infty\) for every \(q\in Q\setminus\{q_0\}\). For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), update \[d_i(q')=\min_{\substack{q\in Q,\ a\in\Sigma:\delta(q,a)=q'}}\bigl(d_{i-1}(q)+c_i(x_i,a)\bigr),\qquad q'\in Q.\] The minimum of an empty set is interpreted as \(+\infty\). Output \(z=\min_{f\in F}d_n(f)\), or \(+\infty\) if no accepting run exists. The output is the minimum additive violation cost of an accepting run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A layered dynamic program computes the cheapest accepting automaton run under position-specific symbol or transition penalties.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) and \(\Sigma\) are finite, \(F\subseteq Q\), and \(\delta:Q\times\Sigma\to Q\) is deterministic.
\(x\in\Sigma^n\), and all transition-use costs are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs the minimum total cost among accepting length-\(n\) runs of \(A\).

notation.meaning: minimum cost of reaching state q after i positions
cost of using automaton symbol a at position i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: This is the standard shortest-path recurrence on a layered finite automaton.

knowledge_statements.title: Soft Scheduling Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduling constraints softened by explicit nonnegative residual penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite activity set, and let \(s_i\) and \(p_i\ge 0\) denote the start time and duration of each activity \(i\in I\). Let \(R\) be a finite index set of hard scheduling predicates \(C_r(s)\), with nonnegative violation functions \(v_r(s)\) satisfying \(v_r(s)=0\iff C_r(s)\). A soft scheduling model introduces \[z=\sum_{r\in R}w_rv_r(s),\qquad w_r>0.\] For example, the precedence predicate \(C_{ij}(s):s_i+p_i\le s_j\) may use \(v_{ij}(s)=\max\{0,s_i+p_i-s_j\}\). The model minimizes or bounds \(z\); imposing \(z=0\) recovers all represented hard scheduling predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft scheduling assigns positive weights to nonnegative violation functions for scheduling predicates and minimizes or bounds their sum; zero aggregate cost recovers every represented hard predicate.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(R\) are finite, \(p_i\ge0\) for every \(i\in I\), and \(w_r>0\) for every \(r\in R\).
Each \(v_r\) is nonnegative and satisfies \(v_r(s)=0\iff C_r(s)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z=0\iff C_r(s)\) holds for every \(r\in R\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost bipartite matching, with optional cardinality or saturation requirements imposed as additional equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Matching optimization selects binary variables \(x_e\in\{0,1\}\) to solve \[\min \sum_{e\in E}c_ex_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{e\in\delta(w)}x_e\le 1\quad(w\in U\cup V).\] The selected set \(M=\{e\in E:x_e=1\}\) is a matching. Replacing selected inequalities by equalities enforces saturation of specified vertices; requiring \(\sum_{e\in E}x_e=k\) enforces cardinality \(k\). Thus the embedded constraint returns an optimal feasible matching and its objective value under the declared side requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose nonincident bipartite edges of minimum total cost, optionally requiring a fixed cardinality or saturation of designated vertices.

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost complete one-to-one assignment on a finite bipartite compatibility graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assignment optimization solves \[\min_{x}\sum_{(i,j)\in E}c_{ij}x_{ij}\] over \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\), subject to \[\sum_{j:(i,j)\in E}x_{ij}=1\quad(i\in I),\qquad \sum_{i:(i,j)\in E}x_{ij}=1\quad(j\in J).\] Thus each agent is assigned to exactly one compatible task and each task to exactly one agent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign every agent to exactly one compatible task and every task to exactly one agent while minimizing total cost.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(J\) are finite sets with \(|I|=|J|\).
Each admissible pair \((i,j)\in E\subseteq I\times J\) has cost \(c_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}\).
The bipartite compatibility graph \((I\cup J,E)\) admits a perfect matching.

knowledge_statements.title: Matching–Assignment Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-preserving correspondence between bipartite matchings and binary vectors satisfying at-most-one assignment constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A binary vector \(x\in\{0,1\}^{E}\) satisfies \[\sum_{j:(i,j)\in E}x_{ij}\le 1\quad(i\in I),\qquad \sum_{i:(i,j)\in E}x_{ij}\le 1\quad(j\in J)\] if and only if \(M_x=\{(i,j)\in E:x_{ij}=1\}\) is a matching. This correspondence is bijective, preserves cardinality, and satisfies \[\sum_{(i,j)\in M_x}c_{ij}=\sum_{(i,j)\in E}c_{ij}x_{ij}.\] Replacing every displayed inequality by equality restricts both sides to perfect matchings and complete one-to-one assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary vectors satisfying the at-most-one assignment constraints correspond bijectively to bipartite matchings and preserve cardinality and cost; equality constraints give perfect assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Shortest-Path Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-source, single-target shortest path represented as a nonnegative unit-flow optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Shortest-path optimization solves \[\min_{x}\sum_{a\in A}c_ax_a\quad\text{subject to}\quad Bx=e_s-e_t,
\qquad x_a\ge 0\quad(a\in A),\] under the incidence convention in which \(e_s-e_t\) represents one unit sent from \(s\) to \(t\). If the graph has no negative-cost directed cycle, the minimum unit-flow value equals the minimum directed \(s\)-to-\(t\) path length, and an optimal solution can be chosen as the incidence vector of such a path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an s-to-t path exists and directed negative-cost cycles are absent, a shortest path can be obtained as a minimum-cost nonnegative unit flow.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonpreemptive job shop with fixed routes and makespan minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The job-shop CP template introduces start variables \(S_{jk}\) and interval variables \(I_{jk}\) of fixed length \(p_{jk}\). Job precedence is imposed by \(S_{j,k+1}\ge S_{jk}+p_{jk}\) for every consecutive pair. For each machine \(m\in M\), the intervals \(\{I_{jk}:m_{jk}=m\}\) satisfy a nonoverlap constraint. The makespan variable satisfies \(C_{\max}\ge S_{jk}+p_{jk}\) for all terminal operations, and the optimization objective is \(\min C_{\max}\). A feasible assignment therefore represents a nonpreemptive schedule respecting every job route and machine capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use interval variables, within-job precedence, and per-machine nonoverlap constraints to model a fixed-route job shop and minimize makespan.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let jobs have operations \(O_{jk}\) ordered by \(k\). Impose \(\operatorname{alternative}(I_{jk},\{I_{jkm}:m\in E_{jk}\})\), so exactly one eligible machine-specific interval is present and shares the master interval's start and end. Impose \(\operatorname{end}(I_{jk})\leq\operatorname{start}(I_{j,k+1})\) and \(\operatorname{noOverlap}(\{I_{jkm}:j,k\})\) for every machine \(m\). A feasible assignment of interval presences and start times is precisely a nonpreemptive flexible job-shop schedule.

knowledge_statements.title: Flow-Shop Templates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonpreemptive flow shop with a common machine route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every job \(j\in J\) contain operations \(O_{j1},\ldots,O_{jq}\), where operation \(O_{jk}\) must run nonpreemptively for \(p_{jk}>0\) on machine \(k\). Introduce interval \(I_{jk}\) with that length. The flow-shop template consists of \(\operatorname{end}(I_{jk})\leq\operatorname{start}(I_{j,k+1})\) for every job and \(k<q\), together with \(\operatorname{noOverlap}(\{I_{jk}:j\in J\})\) for every machine \(k\). Thus all jobs traverse the same ordered machine sequence, while their relative orders on individual machines remain decision variables unless additional permutation constraints are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every job visits the machines in one common order; job precedence and machine no-overlap constraints define feasible schedules.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) and the machine set \(\{1,\ldots,q\}\) are finite.
Each operation is mandatory and nonpreemptive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible interval assignments are exactly the feasible classical flow-shop schedules.

notation.meaning: interval for job j on the kth machine in the common route

children.title: Open-Shop Templates
children.top_down_role: Machine-scheduling compositions without a fixed within-job operation route.

knowledge_statements.title: Open-Shop Templates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonpreemptive open shop with unrestricted within-job operation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each job \(j\in J\) and machine \(m\in M\), let \(I_{jm}\) be a mandatory nonpreemptive interval of length \(p_{jm}>0\). Impose \(\operatorname{noOverlap}(\{I_{jm}:j\in J\})\) for every machine \(m\), and \(\operatorname{noOverlap}(\{I_{jm}:m\in M\})\) for every job \(j\). No precedence relation is imposed among a job's operations. Consequently, machines process at most one job at a time, each job undergoes at most one operation at a time, and the operation order may differ between jobs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each job requires one operation on every machine, but its machine order is free; neither machines nor jobs may process two operations simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) and \(M\) are finite.
All operations are mandatory and nonpreemptive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible interval assignments are exactly the feasible classical open-shop schedules.

notation.meaning: interval for the operation of job j on machine m

children.title: Operation-Ordering Regimes
children.top_down_role: Routing restrictions and sequencing consequences distinguishing flow-shop from open-shop formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Operation-Ordering Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified precedence predicate distinguishing job, flow, open, and permutation regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be the operations and let \(P\subseteq V\times V\) be a strict precedence relation. An operation-ordering regime is specified by requiring \(s_v+p_v\leq s_w\) for every \((v,w)\in P\), together with machine disjunctions \(s_v+p_v\leq s_w\) or \(s_w+p_w\leq s_v\) whenever distinct operations \(v,w\) use the same unary machine. Job shops prescribe a route-specific \(P\); flow shops prescribe one common machine route; open shops prescribe no within-job precedence; permutation flow shops additionally require one common job order on every machine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordering regime selects mandatory precedences and machine disjunctions; different selections yield job-shop, flow-shop, open-shop, or permutation-flow-shop structures.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is acyclic.
Every processing time satisfies \(p_v>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A start-time vector \(s\) respects the regime exactly when all prescribed precedences and unary-machine disjunctions hold.

notation.meaning: prescribed strict precedence relation on operations
start time and processing time of operation v

children.title: Parallel-Machine Templates
children.top_down_role: Scheduling compositions for interchangeable machines with common processing characteristics.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel-Machine Templates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identical parallel machines with optional assignment intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be identical unary machines and let each job \(j\in J\) have machine-independent processing time \(p_j>0\). Create a master interval \(I_j\) and optional intervals \(I_{jm}\) of length \(p_j\) for \(m\in M\). Impose \(\operatorname{alternative}(I_j,\{I_{jm}:m\in M\})\) and, for every \(m\), impose \(\operatorname{noOverlap}(\{I_{jm}:j\in J\})\). Exactly one machine copy is therefore present for each job, and selected copies assigned to the same machine do not overlap. Release dates or deadlines may be represented by domains on the master intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each job chooses exactly one identical machine, retains the same duration on every machine, and cannot overlap another job assigned there.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) and the nonempty machine set \(M\) are finite.
Jobs are nonpreemptive and machines are identical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible interval assignments correspond exactly to feasible identical-parallel-machine schedules.

notation.meaning: optional copy assigning job j to machine m

children.title: Unrelated-Machine Templates
children.top_down_role: Scheduling compositions with machine-dependent processing times or costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Unrelated-Machine Templates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrelated parallel machines with assignment-dependent processing times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each job \(j\in J\) and eligible machine \(m\in E_j\), create an optional interval \(I_{jm}\) of length \(p_{jm}>0\), and create a mandatory master interval \(I_j\). Impose \(\operatorname{alternative}(I_j,\{I_{jm}:m\in E_j\})\) and \(\operatorname{noOverlap}(\{I_{jm}:j\in J,\ m\in E_j\})\) for each machine \(m\). The selected alternative determines both the assigned machine and the job's duration. Unlike identical or uniform parallel machines, the matrix \((p_{jm})\) is unrestricted across jobs and machines.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each job selects one eligible machine; its duration depends arbitrarily on that job-machine pair, and assigned jobs cannot overlap.
assumptions_latex: \(E_j\neq\varnothing\) for every job \(j\).
Jobs are nonpreemptive and each machine is unary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible interval assignments correspond exactly to feasible unrelated-parallel-machine schedules.

children.title: Machine-Eligibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Eligibility restrictions spanning interchangeable, uniform, and unrelated resource settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Machine-Eligibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eligibility predicate for assigning operations to machines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O\) be a finite operation set, \(M\) a finite machine set, and \(E_o\subseteq M\) the allowed machines for operation \(o\). Assignment variables satisfy \(x_{om}\in\{0,1\}\), \(x_{om}=0\) for \(m\notin E_o\), and \(\sum_{m\in E_o}x_{om}=1\). Fixed-machine scheduling has \(|E_o|=1\); complete flexibility has \(E_o=M\); partial flexibility permits arbitrary nonempty proper subsets. If assignment is represented by optional intervals, the equivalent condition is that exactly one interval indexed by \(E_o\) is present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every operation must choose exactly one allowed machine; singleton, full, and intermediate eligible sets encode fixed, complete, and partial flexibility.
assumptions_latex: \(E_o\neq\varnothing\) for every \(o\in O\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An assignment \(x\) is eligibility-feasible exactly when \(\sum_{m\in E_o}x_{om}=1\) and \(x_{om}=0\) outside \(E_o\) for every operation.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Dependent Setup Template
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unary-machine sequencing with predecessor-dependent transition times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each machine \(m\), let \(V_m\) be its assigned operations and let \(s^m_{ij}\geq0\) be the setup time when \(j\) immediately follows \(i\). A sequence variable \(\sigma_m\) orders the present intervals \(I_i\), \(i\in V_m\). Impose a no-overlap constraint with transition matrix \((s^m_{ij})\): whenever \(i\) immediately precedes \(j\) in \(\sigma_m\), require \(\operatorname{start}(I_j)\geq\operatorname{end}(I_i)+s^m_{ij}\). Initial and terminal setup times may be represented by dummy source and sink operations. The matrix need not be symmetric or satisfy the triangle inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A machine sequence is feasible only when consecutive operations are separated by the setup time determined by their ordered pair.
assumptions_latex: Each operation assigned to machine \(m\) is present exactly once in \(\sigma_m\).
Operations are nonpreemptive and \(s^m_{ij}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every consecutive pair \((i,j)\) on machine \(m\) satisfies \(\operatorname{start}(I_j)-\operatorname{end}(I_i)\geq s^m_{ij}\).

notation.meaning: sequence of present operations on machine m
setup time from predecessor i to successor j

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard nonpreemptive RCPSP with renewable resources and precedence constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let activities \(i\in V\) have durations \(p_i\), renewable-resource demands \(a_{ir}\), and precedence arcs \(A\). Introduce start times \(s_i\) and intervals \(I_i=[s_i,s_i+p_i)\). Impose \(s_i+p_i\leq s_j\) for every \((i,j)\in A\), and for every renewable resource \(r\) and time \(t\), impose \(\sum_{i:t\in I_i}a_{ir}\leq C_r\). With a dummy terminal activity, minimizing its start time minimizes the project makespan. These constraints define the standard nonpreemptive resource-constrained project scheduling problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activities obey a precedence DAG and, throughout execution, their simultaneous renewable-resource demand cannot exceed capacity; the usual objective minimizes makespan.
assumptions_latex: \((V,A)\) is a finite acyclic digraph.
\(p_i\geq0\), \(a_{ir}\geq0\), and \(C_r\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A start-time vector is feasible exactly when all precedence and renewable-capacity inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: demand of activity i for renewable resource r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical nonpreemptive renewable-resource RCPSP formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The renewable-resource RCPSP formulation is standard and fits the leaf, but no inspectable authoritative citation is supplied for the formulation and exact feasibility claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Mode Project Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-mode RCPSP with mode-dependent duration and resource use.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each activity \(i\), let \(K_i\) be its finite mode set. Mode \(k\in K_i\) has duration \(p_{ik}\), renewable demand \(a_{ikr}\), and nonrenewable demand \(b_{ikq}\). Select exactly one mode using \(y_{ik}\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\sum_{k\in K_i}y_{ik}=1\). The selected mode determines the activity interval's length and demands. Impose project precedences, renewable cumulative constraints \(\sum_{i:t\in I_i}\sum_k a_{ikr}y_{ik}\leq C_r\), and nonrenewable budgets \(\sum_i\sum_k b_{ikq}y_{ik}\leq B_q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each activity chooses one execution mode, which determines its duration and demands; precedence, renewable capacities, and nonrenewable budgets must all hold.
assumptions_latex: Every mode set \(K_i\) is finite and nonempty.
The precedence graph is acyclic and activities are nonpreemptive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A mode selection and schedule are feasible exactly when the exactly-one, precedence, renewable-capacity, and nonrenewable-budget constraints hold.

notation.meaning: indicator that activity i uses mode k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multi-mode formulation is plausible and appropriately represented, but the precise renewable and nonrenewable resource conventions require an authoritative, claim-specific source.

knowledge_statements.title: Optional-Activity Project Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Profit-weighted project scheduling with optional activities and precedence closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each activity \(i\) with a presence variable \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\), optional interval \(I_i\), profit \(w_i\), and resource demands \(a_{ir}\). Enforce \(\operatorname{presence}(I_i)=z_i\). For every prerequisite arc \((i,j)\), impose \(z_j\leq z_i\) and, when \(z_j=1\), impose \(\operatorname{end}(I_i)\leq\operatorname{start}(I_j)\). Resource cumulative constraints count only present intervals. Maximizing \(\sum_i w_i z_i\), possibly subject to a deadline or makespan bound, selects a precedence-closed, resource-feasible activity portfolio and its schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optional activities earn profit when selected; selection must include prerequisites, and only selected intervals consume resources and obey conditional timing constraints.
assumptions_latex: The prerequisite graph is acyclic.
Each selected activity is nonpreemptive and has fixed demand during execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected set \(\{i:z_i=1\}\) is precedence-closed and admits the represented resource-feasible schedule.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard optional-interval and precedence-closure encoding
objective and dependency conventions vary across project-selection models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Optional-activity and precedence-closure conventions vary, and without a deadline, makespan bound, or other coupling condition the portfolio interpretation may become degenerate. An authoritative source is required to establish the intended model variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Production Scheduling with Calendars
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calendar-aware scheduling permitting processing suspension during unavailable periods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each resource \(r\), let \(C_r(t)\geq0\) be its time-varying capacity. For each activity \(i\), let \(u_i(t)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether processing occurs at time \(t\), and require \(u_i(t)=0\) whenever its assigned machine or required calendar is unavailable. Impose \(\int_{s_i}^{e_i}u_i(t)\,dt=p_i\) and \(\sum_i a_{ir}u_i(t)\leq C_r(t)\) for every \(r,t\). Precedence requires \(e_i\leq s_j\) on each arc \((i,j)\). Calendar interruptions extend elapsed duration without reducing required processing effort.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activities accumulate processing only during available periods; time-varying capacities constrain simultaneous work, and calendar interruptions lengthen elapsed execution.
assumptions_latex: Calendar functions are measurable and piecewise constant on a finite scheduling horizon.
Processing may pause at calendar closures but not at arbitrary available times unless separately permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A schedule is feasible when each activity receives processing measure \(p_i\), respects calendars and precedences, and never exceeds \(C_r(t)\).
review_flags: preemption and calendar-interruption conventions require source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed intensity formulation permits processing to pause at arbitrary available times, while the assumptions permit pauses only at calendar closures. A source and corrected formal restriction are needed to determine the intended calendar-preemption semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Nurse-Rostering Template
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon, single-shift-per-day feasibility template with coverage, workload, qualification, and transition constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{nds}\in\{0,1\}\). A nurse roster is feasible when
\[
\sum_{s\in S}x_{nds}\le 1\quad(n\in N,d\in D),
\]
\[
\sum_{n\in N}q_{ns}x_{nds}\ge r_{ds}\quad(d\in D,s\in S),
\]
\[
L_n\le\sum_{d\in D}\sum_{s\in S}x_{nds}\le U_n\quad(n\in N),
\]
and
\[
x_{nds}+x_{n,d+1,t}\le1
\quad(n\in N,d\in\{1,\ldots,H-1\},(s,t)\in F).
\]
Thus each nurse receives at most one daily shift, qualified coverage meets demand, workloads remain bounded, and forbidden transitions do not occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign nurses to daily shifts so that qualified demand is covered, daily assignments are unique, workloads stay within bounds, and forbidden consecutive shifts are avoided.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) and \(S\) are finite sets of nurses and shifts, and \(D=\{1,\ldots,H\}\) for an integer \(H\ge1\).
\(r_{ds}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), \(q_{ns}\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0\le L_n\le U_n\) are given.
\(F\subseteq S\times S\) contains forbidden consecutive-shift pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is characterized by the displayed assignment, coverage, workload, and transition constraints.

notation.meaning: one when nurse n works shift s on day d
required qualified coverage on day d and shift s

knowledge_statements.title: Workforce Shift-Scheduling Template
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite workforce assignment with availability, skill coverage, individual hour limits, and shift conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{wt}\in\{0,1\}\). The workforce shift-scheduling template consists of
\[
x_{wt}\le a_{wt}\quad(w\in W,t\in T),
\]
\[
\sum_{w\in W}q_{wk}x_{wt}\ge r_{tk}\quad(t\in T,k\in K),
\]
\[
\sum_{t\in T}h_t x_{wt}\le H_w\quad(w\in W),
\]
and
\[
x_{wt}+x_{wu}\le1\quad(w\in W,\{t,u\}\in E).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign available, qualified workers to shifts, cover every skill demand, respect hour limits, and prevent each worker from taking conflicting shifts.
assumptions_latex: \(W,T,K\) are finite sets of workers, shifts, and skills.
\(a_{wt},q_{wk}\in\{0,1\}\), \(r_{tk}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and \(h_t\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) are given.
\(H_w\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) is a finite hour limit for each \(w\in W\).
\(E\subseteq\{\{t,u\}:t,u\in T,t\ne u\}\) is the set of conflicting shift pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The binary matrix \(x\) is a feasible workforce shift schedule exactly when it satisfies all displayed constraints.

notation.meaning: one when worker w is assigned to shift t
availability of worker w for shift t
qualification of worker w for skill k

knowledge_statements.title: Course-Timetabling Template
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-meeting course assignment to one room-period, with room capacity and pairwise conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{cpr}\in\{0,1\}\). The course-timetabling template is
\[
\sum_{p\in P}\sum_{r\in R}x_{cpr}=1\quad(c\in C),
\]
\[
\sum_{c\in C}x_{cpr}\le1\quad(p\in P,r\in R),
\]
\[
u_c x_{cpr}\le b_r\quad(c\in C,p\in P,r\in R),
\]
and
\[
\sum_{r\in R}x_{cpr}+\sum_{r\in R}x_{c'pr}\le1
\quad(p\in P,\{c,c'\}\in E).
\]
The constraints assign every course once, enforce exclusive room use and adequate room capacity, and separate conflicting courses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Place every course in one room-period while preventing room collisions, respecting room capacities, and separating conflicting courses.
assumptions_latex: \(C,P,R\) are finite sets of courses, periods, and rooms.
\(u_c\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is the enrollment of course \(c\), and \(b_r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is the capacity of room \(r\).
\(E\subseteq\{\{c,c'\}:c,c'\in C,c\ne c'\}\) records course conflicts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A binary array \(x\) satisfying the displayed constraints defines a conflict-free, capacity-feasible course timetable.

notation.meaning: one when course c is placed in period p and room r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical assignment-and-conflict timetabling template; assignment locator is indirect

knowledge_statements.title: Examination-Timetabling Template
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-room examination assignment with candidate-conflict separation, exclusive room use, and capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y_{xpr}\in\{0,1\}\). The examination-timetabling template requires
\[
\sum_{p\in P}\sum_{r\in R}y_{xpr}=1\quad(x\in X),
\]
\[
\sum_{x\in X}y_{xpr}\le1\quad(p\in P,r\in R),
\]
\[
m_x y_{xpr}\le b_r\quad(x\in X,p\in P,r\in R),
\]
and
\[
\sum_{r\in R}y_{xpr}+\sum_{r\in R}y_{x'pr}\le1
\quad(p\in P,\{x,x'\}\in E).
\]
Hence each examination occurs once, no room hosts two examinations simultaneously, assigned rooms are large enough, and examinations sharing candidates occur in different periods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign each examination to one room-period, give it sufficient capacity, prevent simultaneous room use, and separate examinations sharing candidates.
assumptions_latex: \(X,P,R\) are finite sets of examinations, periods, and rooms.
\(m_x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is the enrollment of examination \(x\), and \(b_r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is the capacity of room \(r\).
\(E\subseteq\{\{x,x'\}:x,x'\in X,x\ne x'\}\) is the set of examination pairs sharing at least one candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraints characterize single-room examination timetables without candidate conflicts or room-capacity violations.

notation.meaning: one when examination x uses period p and room r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical assignment-and-conflict examination template; assignment locator is indirect

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern-Based Roster Template
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-covering roster formulation using nurse-specific, prevalidated complete work patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(n\in N\) and \(p\in P_n\), let \(y_{np}\in\{0,1\}\). A pattern-based roster satisfies
\[
\sum_{p\in P_n}y_{np}=1\quad(n\in N)
\]
and
\[
\sum_{n\in N}\sum_{p\in P_n}a_{npds}y_{np}\ge r_{ds}
\quad(d\in D,s\in S).
\]
Every pattern in \(P_n\) is assumed to encode all nurse-local rules, such as rest, shift succession, and workload bounds. Consequently, the master constraints select one admissible pattern per nurse and cover aggregate staffing demand.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one prevalidated work pattern for each nurse so that the combined patterns cover every day-shift staffing requirement.
assumptions_latex: \(N,D,S\) are finite sets of nurses, days, and shifts.
Each nurse \(n\in N\) has a finite admissible pattern set \(P_n\).
\(r_{ds}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(a_{npds}\in\{0,1\}\) are given for all applicable indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected patterns form a feasible roster precisely when the assignment and coverage constraints hold, provided every \(P_n\) contains only patterns satisfying the nurse-local rules.

notation.meaning: one when pattern p is selected for nurse n
one when nurse n's pattern p covers shift s on day d
required staffing on day d and shift s
